https://claude.ai/code/artifact/344c5a6c-2da1-44ef-87c7-2b4e978f154f 

**Benchmark numbers are promising but don't paint this as a slam dunk:**



Custom Metrics

Three numbers for "did the extraction keep the page's content, and nothing else."
Everything is computed on **normalized** text, so markdown, emphasis, quotes,
dashes, whitespace and rendered-vs-LaTeX math (`κ` = `\kappa`) never count as a
difference.

Let $G$ be the gold text and $P$ the prediction.

- $S(x)$ = the **set of 5-grams** of $\text{normalize}(x)$
- $U(G)$ = the **sentences of $G$** with at least 8 words

## KEPT — recall

Fraction of gold's sentences that survive. A sentence counts as kept if at least
half of its 5-grams appear anywhere in the prediction:

$$\text{KEPT} = \frac{1}{|U(G)|}\sum_{u \in U(G)} \mathbb{1}\!\left[\frac{|S(u) \cap S(P)|}{|S(u)|} \ge 0.5\right]$$

Sentences shorter than 5 words can't form a 5-gram, so they're matched by direct
substring containment instead.

## CLEAN — precision

Fraction of what we emitted that actually exists in gold:

$$\text{CLEAN} = \frac{|S(P) \cap S(G)|}{|S(P)|}$$

## FIDELITY — the headline

F-score of the two, with **recall weighted twice as heavily** as precision
($\beta^2 = 2$), because dropping content is worse than keeping extra:

$$\text{FIDELITY} = \frac{(1+\beta^2)\cdot \text{CLEAN} \cdot \text{KEPT}}{\beta^2 \cdot \text{CLEAN} + \text{KEPT}} = \frac{3\cdot \text{CLEAN}\cdot \text{KEPT}}{2\cdot \text{CLEAN} + \text{KEPT}}$$

The same construction gives **CODE**, **MATH**, **TABLE** and **WHO** — identical
to KEPT, but with $U(G)$ replaced by gold's code lines, math expressions, table
cells, or speaker names.




Overall I think our new spec is better but it wasn't as easy to hill climb this as I had hoped.

Details Spec-Driven Mix: Surprisingly it doesn't move DCLM that much, although it makes HQ competitive with DCLM: Fully inverts the OLMO scores though when you mix for DCLM instead:
--- --- **BLEnD Cultural QA:** From here: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.09948
Details Spec-Driven Mix: Interestingly the DCLM data is better for cultural QA than our old spec, but I suspect our new spec will be better: I also suspect this might have more to do with models being good at in-context MCQ than cultural understanding
---
---
The Problem with DCLM Core DCLM Disaggregated: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/dc5f1cf5-eb62-4c99-9e2f-70472b28797e OLMO Disaggregated: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/ce4e61f6-f3e9-433b-ae76-805a12015ee5 DCLM Core is super noisy. Some are higher signal (basically hellaswag), and with mixing we can improve over Hellaswag: But many **many** are just noise, and no sense of trying to win on them at this scale: In contrast OLMO bpb seems to be pretty high signal: Although there are some that are still noisy here too: My thought: **maybe we forget about DCLM Core and showcase wins on OLMO Base Easy instead at least for spec-driven project at smaller scale** This is where we already win, no new specs, no mixing needed!
---
Distillation Progress Distilling back into our FastText -> ModernBERT -> Resiliparse/JustText pipeline for LLM_Curated_v1.1. **FastText**: **ModernBERT**: Still training - ModernBERT 1M: 40.3% (step 1,575 / 3,906) — on pace to finish tonight, F1 lands right after in its end-of-run eval. - ModernBERT 10M: 11.1% (step 4,317 / 39,062) — the multi-day flagship, pace steady at ~5s/step, ETA roughly 2 days out. **Resiliparse (instead of JustText since it is faster)**:
---
Plan **Experiment Idea**: Scale everything down by 20x. So instead of a 100B model we are training a 5B, and instead of nemotron producing 7T tokes we sample 350B tokens. And instead of a 2T token target or similar we have a 200B token target. Once I extract 5% of the internet I will have about 3-4T tokens or so. We would be comparing 350B tokens of nemotron to 2T tokens of my data, on a 200B token target for a 5B model. We can do whatever data mixing we choose but at the end of the day we need to find the best 200B tokens to train that 5B model. This seems like the most fair way to compare the data at smaller scale and should be achievable within a week or so of launching my big run.
---

# Weekly Sync 8/31-9/4 ---
"Hero" Data Curation Run Progress We currently have about 10T tokens of pre-dedupe data processed! This will be significantly lower after dedupe, but dedupe alone now takes many hours (days?) to run, so I don't have timely feedback about how much data we have post-dedupe. **Updated this morning:**
> [!TIP] > The run is about 15% of the way through and will finish in the next 2 weeks if I don't steal my compute for other experiments. ---
More principled FLOP estimation ## Inference FLOPs of the fast curation cascade **Estimate: 1.3e10 to 1.7e10 FLOPs per extracted document, 5.1e14 to 6.7e14 per WARC, and 4.0e21 to 5.3e21 for the 8M-WARC run (7,925,398 WARCs).** The low end charges each document its real token count; the high end charges the padded length the chip actually runs. ettin68 accounts for 98% of the total. | | Actual lengths | Padded lengths | |---|---|---| | Per extracted doc | 1.3e10 | 1.7e10 | | Per kept doc | 6.9e10 | 9.0e10 | | Per WARC | 5.1e14 | 6.7e14 | | Per kept token (ModernBERT tokens) | 5.1e7 | 6.7e7 | | 8M run total | 4.0e21 | 5.3e21 | The rest of this note explains how the numbers are produced. The deployed pipeline (`lpv11_fastpipe_v2_1_fused`) scores every extracted document with three classifiers in sequence: fastText, a pooled super-token transformer, and ettin68. Each stage only sees the documents the previous stage passed on, so the cost per document is an expectation over the stages a document reaches. ### Stages and reach rates | Stage | Model | Context | Condition to run | Share of extracted docs | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | fastText w640 | full doc | always | 100% | | 2 | pooled transformer (90M-doc ckpt) | 8192 | fastText prob ≥ 0.0048 | 58.2% | | 3 | ettin68 | 2048 | pooled prob in [0.079, 0.8883) | 20.1% | Of the documents the pooled model scores, 18.3% are accepted outright, 47.2% are dropped, and 34.6% go to ettin68. Overall, 19.2% of extracted documents are kept. Rates are measured from production catalogs (52 shards, 12,824 WARCs). Per WARC: 39,464 records, 38,560 extracted docs, 22,423 fastText survivors, 7,749 band docs, 7,413 kept docs. ## Expected cost per document ``` E[FLOPs per extracted doc] = c_ft + p_ft * E[ c_pool(min(L, 8192)) | passed fastText ] + p_ft * p_band * E[ c_ettin(min(L, 2048)) | in band ] p_ft = 0.5815 p_band = 0.3456 ``` Each stage's cost is averaged over the token-length distribution of the documents that actually reach it. Those distributions come from the 100k comparison sample, which stores every stage's score per document: we tokenize its deployment text with the ModernBERT tokenizer and apply the production thresholds. The sample's reach rates match production within two points. **How padding works.** Within a WARC, the scorer sorts a stage's documents by length, takes batches of 32, and pads each batch to the smallest bucket in (128, 256, ..., context) that fits the longest document in that batch. The last batch is filled to 32 rows with empty rows. Because batches are length-sorted, all 32 documents in a batch are close in length, so the padded cost is well approximated by charging each document its own bucket; simulating the real per-batch procedure on the sample gives the same mean within 1%. Padding raises the mean charged length by 1.37x for the pooled stage and 1.30x for ettin68, which is the gap between the two columns below and in the headline table. | Stage | Reach rate | Mean tokens, actual (capped at context) | Mean tokens, padded | Cost per doc, actual | Cost per doc, padded | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | fastText | 100% | 1,318 (no cap) | n/a | 2.0e5 | 2.0e5 | | pooled | 58.2% | 1,010 | 1,380 | 4.1e8 | 5.7e8 | | ettin68 | 20.1% | 608 | 792 | 6.5e10 | 8.5e10 | ## 8M run document counts (7,925,398 WARCs) | | Count | |---|---| | Docs scored by fastText | 3.1e11 | | Docs scored by pooled | 1.8e11 | | Docs scored by ettin68 | 6.1e10 | | Kept docs | 5.9e10 | For reference, 4.0e21 to 5.3e21 FLOPs is the 6ND training cost of a 1B model on 700B to 900B tokens. ## Caveats - FLOPs and chip time diverge. Measured chip time from the catalogs implies MFU of 0.1 to 0.4% for the pooled stage and 1.4 to 5.7% for ettin68. All-in, the run is 26.2 v6e-8 slice-seconds per WARC (about 58k slice-hours for 8M WARCs), which is 0.35% MFU against the FLOP total. - fastText FLOPs count arithmetic only. Its measured cost is 0.55 CPU-ms per document, mostly hashing and table lookups. - Token counts use the ModernBERT tokenizer, not the training tokenizer. - Reach rates are from the current ladder's crawl mix.
Conventions - Forward pass only; a multiply-add counts as 2 FLOPs. - Embedding lookups, layer norms, softmax, activations, and the pooling reduction count as zero. - Length `L` includes the two special tokens and is capped at the stage context. The padded variant rounds `L` up to the next bucket in (128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192). - Empty tail rows in a WARC's last batch are included in the per-batch simulation and add under 1%.
fastText formula dim 100, word bigrams, no character n-grams (read from the model header). Features are words plus bigrams, about twice the word count; words are taken as 0.75 of ModernBERT tokens. One add per dimension per feature, then a 100 x 2 output layer. ``` F = 2 * 0.75 * T c_ft = 100 * F + 2 * 100 * 2 ≈ 150 T + 400 ``` At T = 1,318 this is 2.0e5.
Pooled transformer formula Levanter's `PooledTransformerConfig.flops_per_token`, called directly. `L` padded tokens, `S = L / 64` super-tokens, hidden `D = 512`, pooled input width 768 (mean, max, min of 256-dim embeddings), feed-forward 2048, 4 layers, 2 labels. ``` proj = 2 * 768 * D * S layer = 2 * 4 * D^2 * S # q, k, v, o projections + 2 * 2 * S^2 * D # QK^T and AV + 2 * 2 * D * 2048 * S # MLP head = 2 * D * 2 c_pool(L) = proj + 4 * layer + head ``` About 4.1e5 FLOPs per input token, nearly flat in `L`.
ettin68 formula Hand-derived (Levanter's generic helper adds a vocabulary-head term a classifier does not have). Hidden `D = 512`, GeGLU feed-forward 768, 19 layers, 8 heads, global attention on every third layer starting at layer 0 (7 layers), sliding window 128 on the other 12. ``` linear_per_token_per_layer = 2 * 4 * D^2 # q, k, v, o + 2 * D * 2 * 768 # GeGLU up and gate + 2 * 768 * D # down attn_per_token_per_layer = 4 * span * D # span = L (global), min(L, 128) (local) c_ettin(L) = L * sum over 19 layers of (linear + attn) ``` Linear term 8.5e7 per token (two times the 42M non-embedding parameters); attention 3.2e7 at L = 2048; total 1.17e8 per token.
Data sources - Reach rates and per-WARC counts: fused catalogs, 52 random shards of the 404 to 8079 ladder. - Per-stage length distributions: 100k comparison sample (`extractor_compare/high_quality_200warc`), deployment text tokenized with `answerdotai/ModernBERT-base`, production thresholds applied to stored scores. - Model shapes: checkpoint `config.json` for pooled 90M and ettin68; fastText hyperparameters from the model binary header. - Chip time: catalog columns `pooled_s` and `score_s` times device count, per device type.
> [!TIP] > The distilled pipeline is projected to take about 5e21 flops to run on the full 8M WARC files. > The previous 8B model running on all of the internet was projected to take between 3e25 and 1.8e26 flops depending on if I used the pipeline version or the single call spec. > The fact that it is taking a month is likely somewhat due to poor MFU ---
Updated Main Results from Mixing
> [!TIP] > Finally showing signs of how the "more data" really helps at scale (100B+ tokens) ---
Beta Paper Outline Old Paper: https://www.overleaf.com/read/krtygrzdmrzc#9088c4 New Paper (extremely preliminary for now, will auto-update here): https://www.overleaf.com/read/tzzfngmmyqsp#daf616 **Introduction:** Something about how we should spend way more compute on data curation but it doesn't need to be more complicated. **Background**: Current data curation pipelines including data mixing **Method**: Spec-Driven Curation, as well as the distillation into FastText, Pooled Transformer, and Ettin68 (modernBERT) **Swapping the spec enables control of the data distribution**: We show different specs lead to expected changes in data downstream
Plots
We then argue that because of the mixing and the growing demand for tokens we opt to use the coverage spec. **Spec-Driven Curation Yields Bigger and Better Data**: We show that by using our high coverage spec distilled pipeline we get more data and can mix it to be better at many domains.
Plots **Bigger**: Everything else bends upwards, but we can train on 100B+ tokens from just 10k WARCs. If we 800x (which is a bad way to do this bc no accounting for dedup), then we should be able to train on 80T tokens without issue. **Better Coverage**: We can mix for several downstream target capabilities.
**Ablations**: When we remove parts of the system how much does it impact performance. All ablations will be done on the olmo base easy eval set.
Plots **THESE ARE JUST STAND IN PLOTS, I HAVE TO RUN THESE EXPERIMENTS:** **Original Resiliparse vs Our "AutoResearch" Resiliparse**: **Spec for Quality ("High Quality") vs Spec for Coverage ("High Coverage")**: **Distilled Pipeline into Classifiers vs Original**: **Mixing vs No Mixing**:
**Discussion**: Scaling this up to the full internet **Conclusion**: Invest more flops into the pretraining data curation.

issues.author: ravwojdyla-agent
issues.body:
## TL;DR Run a five-day spike to post-train a Snowball specialist for Python problems with executable tests. Start from the pinned September 23 supervised fine-tuning (SFT) checkpoint. Run the coding tasks through `lib/shellbox`, with ShellSim as the first environment backend. Measure coding improvement, export a teacher, and verify its use in multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). The four-update pilot failed its development gate, so the sealed final set and MOPD stayed closed. The spike completed as a negative result. ## Description A coding expert is a specialized Snowball checkpoint. MOPD combines domain teachers by routing student-generated responses to the appropriate teacher for token scores. This spike supplies and validates the coding teacher. Use [open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-GLM53-RLVR-SFT-2026.09.23](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-GLM53-RLVR-SFT-2026.09.23/tree/227263f32121ac79ba96de6136b86221e58b05db) at revision `227263f32121ac79ba96de6136b86221e58b05db`. This is the latest published Snowball SFT checkpoint found on September 29. It continues the September 21 Datakit SFT model with 5,000 GLM 5.3 conversations and 136 supervised updates. The RLVR term in its name describes the source conversations. Pin its tokenizer and chat template with the weights. Use this parent for the frozen baseline, coding specialist, and controlled MOPD student experiment. Establish fresh baseline scores. The earlier mixed-RLVR Step92 results do not describe this parent. The implementation can reuse these components: - [Curriculum coding SFT](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/871b505121ba2730033e802dd4370825ac0d4ca1/experiments/post_training/curriculum_sft/code_trial.py): task generation, execution checks, verified solution selection, training, export, and evaluation. Its current four-step recipe uses a different parent. - [Marin RL artifacts](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/871b505121ba2730033e802dd4370825ac0d4ca1/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/skyrl.py): explicit role geometry, model and data dependencies, and HF export. Keep experiment composition in `experiments/post_training/coding_expert*.py`. - [`lib/shellbox`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/562d705673859548c58b46d8f2383ab8a053797f/lib/shellbox): persistent Harbor shell environments and the external `BashAgent`. - [Grug TaskCompendium smoke](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9527): the current pinned-HF and Megatron base for this spike. PR #9507 is broader workflow migration work and is not a prerequisite. - [Snowball MOPD smoke](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/749): four completed updates with three teachers on 64 H100s. That result excludes benchmark improvement and HF conversion validation. The implementation starts from PR #9527 and pins MarinSkyRL `e26273f7968cf124cc667372b3147da5b6c7a0cf`. This runtime supports the terminal-bench Harbor runner, Megatron training, a ShellSim-aware launch preflight, and explicit custom Harbor agent import paths. The spike pins the parent, tokenizer, Shellbox revision, ShellSim version, task data, and runtime before each run. Prepare approximately 2,000–5,000 training problems, subject to the source audit. Reserve separate development and final sets before model-based screening. Keep variants of one problem in the same split. Remove benchmark overlap and check overlap with the parent's additional GLM SFT corpus. Record source revisions, problem IDs, verifier settings, and rejected rows. These checks do not establish absence from pretraining. Materialize each selected problem as a Harbor task package. The task gives the agent a persistent Shellbox Bash session and asks it to write `/workspace/solution.py`. Private tests execute the file against the pinned standard-input or function-call cases. The verifier writes binary reward only after all tests pass. Do not put private tests or expected outputs in the agent-visible environment. Use `shellbox.backends.shellsim.environment:ShellSimEnvironment` and `shellbox.agent:BashAgent` for the smoke and pilot. ShellSim 0.1.20 provides simulated `python` and `pytest`, so it can run these tasks without a Docker image or network. Run known-pass and known-fail canaries before model rollouts. Harbor uploads private tests only after the agent turn. The custom verifier downloads the submitted program and private cases after that upload, then starts a separate host subprocess and a fresh ShellSim Python process for each case. This keeps the agent session out of the verifier and contains ShellSim child timeouts. Treat the reward as exploratory and recheck the selected candidate on public code evaluations and a clean held-out execution path before a capability claim. Start with code-only reinforcement learning from the SFT parent. Use the terminal-bench Harbor entrypoint so each rollout can edit files and run tests through Shellbox. Use a short verified-SFT warmup only if the pilot lacks successful solutions or valid tool calls. Initial candidates are 64 prompts per update, four samples per prompt, one update epoch, and learning rate `5e-7`. Bound the run to approximately 20–60 updates and a fixed compute limit. The one-update smoke and pilot measurements determine the final settings before the full training run. Use binary reward for passing all tests. Record verifier, agent, and infrastructure failures separately from incorrect programs. Measure turn-cap exits, response length, tool-call validity, test failures, and groups that contain different rewards. Earlier mixed-domain Snowball runs lost coding signal through output truncation and constant-zero reward groups ([trace audit](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/507)). The shared SFT trial also records destructive math updates at high learning rates ([results](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/871b505121ba2730033e802dd4370825ac0d4ca1/experiments/post_training/curriculum_sft/README.md)). These are reasons for bounded pilots and frequent evaluation. ## Hypothesis or Goal Short, execution-verified post-training can improve held-out Python correctness and produce a teacher that supplies valid MOPD evidence. Primary metric: held-out coding pass@1 at a fixed generation budget. Target a gain of at least five percentage points over the frozen SFT parent. Report paired uncertainty across problems. Treat this threshold as a research target, not a forecast. Supporting evaluations: HumanEval+, MBPP+, and CRUXEval output. Use thinking off and explicit settings from the [September 24 evaluation policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9409). Label shorter internal evaluations separately. Measure MATH-500 and IFBench at the parent, expert, and distilled-student stages to record changes outside coding. Teacher acceptance requires an HF reload, matching tokenizer fingerprints, finite token scores, and exact alignment with the student's generated tokens. Start with chosen-token evidence and `sampled_reverse_kl` under the [existing OPD contract](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/3b620d8b2bc2ac927d1e4b7004e2d456474e714a/skyrl-train/docs/algorithms/opd.rst). Add an explicit `code` route. The existing smoke's `swe` route also contains tool-call tasks, so the new expert must not replace that route without a data change. Hold the other teachers fixed. If compute permits, compare matched student updates with the SFT parent versus the new expert as coding teacher. Finite loss proves integration only. A transfer claim requires improved student evaluation results. A candidate qualifies for teacher integration after a positive held-out pass@1 point estimate and successful teacher acceptance checks. Report gains whose paired interval includes zero as unresolved. The five-point target remains the target for a useful coding expert. ## Status The source audit is complete. Artifact `2026.09.29.2` accepted 5,567 problems after gold-solution ShellSim preflight and contains 2,400 training, 300 development, and 300 sealed final tasks. Its published runtime bundle includes ShellSim's `_native.abi3.so`. Artifact `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/rav/documents/snowball-python-expert/2026.09.29.3` completed with the first ShellSim-aware MarinSkyRL pin, but its launcher fix read the wrong resolved-config field. Replacement artifact `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/rav/documents/snowball-python-expert/2026.09.29.4` completed in 7 minutes 18 seconds with corrected MarinSkyRL commit `92fbe5126329c38659b54913424e64c39bbeab89`. Its manifest has fingerprint `9dd2b7ad`, and the artifact contains 15,040 staged files. It pins source data, tokenizer, Shellbox commit [`c96bf413`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/c96bf413031fdde2fea1cfd30b4133b44c959a8c), ShellSim 0.1.20, the custom environment, and verifier. The earlier artifacts are superseded for training. The first frozen-parent public evaluation is complete. HumanEval+ pass@1 is 51.83%, MBPP+ pass@1 is 42.06%, CRUXEval input pass@1 is 4.63%, and CRUXEval output pass@1 is 8.88%. The record contains valid aggregate metrics but reports zero graded samples because the archive does not map each task's count field (#9538). A later matched rerun of the same parent produced different scores despite an equal artifact model config and the same evaluation seed (#9558). Do not compare the candidate to this first record. Use the matched parent and candidate artifacts below. A direct-verifier smoke produced 10.55% sample reward and 21.88% pass@4, then failed during the first optimizer update because the policy and KL reference filled one 80 GiB H100. That run produced no checkpoint. A lower-memory rerun was canceled after the environment changed to Shellbox. The next gate is one Shellbox Megatron update, checkpoint, HF export, and reload. The Shellbox path has confirmed runtime gaps and bounded workarounds. The pinned SkyRL image does not include Shellbox or ShellSim (#9532), so the data artifact carries their pinned runtime packages, including ShellSim's native module. The first workaround for custom `BashAgent` selection changed Harbor's shared named-agent map during environment import. Pilot 6 confirmed that this has a concurrent-start race (#9533). MarinSkyRL commit `e26273f79` exposes `AgentConfig.import_path`, rejects a conflicting named agent, and passed all 17 focused builder tests. The recipe now selects `shellbox.agent:BashAgent` through this explicit field. A ShellSim child timeout can terminate its parent trial (#9535), so verification runs in a separate host subprocess. Local metadata can select a missing storage bucket (#9536), so data preparation runs from a CoreWeave coordinator with the mapped S3 prefix. Local graph compilation did not reject a derived Harbor turn limit (#9542), so the recipe now passes the pinned runtime parser before launch. The launcher also treated every terminal-bench run as Daytona (#9543). The first workaround read `skyrl.terminal_bench` and failed again before H100 allocation because the resolved schema uses `skyrl.terminal_bench_config`. Corrected MarinSkyRL commit `92fbe512` uses the resolved field, and all 13 focused preflight tests pass. Smoke 4 passed launch preflight and allocated five H100×8 nodes. The 32-rank Megatron policy and eight-way vLLM service initialized, all four Harbor rollout workers started, and training entered global step 0. All observed rollout batches then failed 0/4 before generation because `BashAgent` sent Harbor's `hosted_vllm/` alias to the strict vLLM endpoint (#9546). Inspection also confirmed that `BashAgent` did not forward the configured 4,096-token call limit (#9548), and ShellSim could not copy agent logs to the remote S3 target (#9547). The run was canceled after 23 minutes to release 40 H100s. It produced no optimizer update, checkpoint, or export. Shellbox commits `739c5c052` and `cb4a330d9` normalize direct model requests, forward the LLM call settings, and stage remote log downloads through a local directory. Four focused Shellbox tests, 27 recipe and SkyRL tests, Ruff, Pyrefly, the repository pre-commit checks, and the lint catalog review pass. Artifact `2026.09.29.5` completed in 7 minutes 45 seconds and pins Shellbox `cb4a330d9`. Its remote root contains the train, development, and final splits, runtime packages, artifact metadata, and provenance. Smoke 5 completed the one-update training and export gate. The 32-rank Megatron policy and eight-way vLLM service initialized on 40 H100s. All five training tasks succeeded in about 19 minutes. Rollout batches completed, including 4/4 batches, and observed task rewards included both zero and one. The optimizer reached `global_step=1` and wrote its checkpoint. The export job then loaded that checkpoint on four H100×8 nodes, wrote 79 Hugging Face safetensor shards, and verified that the shard index references a complete set. The terminal record is `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/rav/checkpoints/snowball-python-expert-smoke/2026.09.29.5/terminal.json`; the policy export is `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/rav/checkpoints/snowball-python-expert-smoke/2026.09.29.5/exports/global_step_1/policy`. The model also emitted undeclared tool names. `BashAgent` ended those trials instead of letting the model correct its action (#9554). Shellbox commit `ee9e2b9f0` now returns a structured error for an unsupported name and keeps the Bash-only execution boundary. Artifact `2026.09.29.6` completed with fingerprint `2bc9e23d` and this exact pin. Smoke 6 training succeeded at `/rav/snowball-python-expert-shellbox-smoke-6-coord/users-rav-checkpoints-snowball-python-expert-smoke-2026.09.29.6-7492a47bf176`: all five H100×8 tasks completed without a failure or retry in about 19 minutes. Repeated rollout batches completed 4/4, and the run logged both zero rewards and at least 13 reward-one trajectories. Its four-node export also succeeded in about 14 minutes and wrote the expected 79 shards. Commit `1865ae43e` adds a bounded reload stage that serves the real export and runs one evaluation item. Coordinator `/rav/snowball-python-expert-reload-smoke-6-coord` succeeded; its H100×8 evaluation loaded the smoke 6 export in vLLM and served the request. The update, checkpoint, export, and reload gate is complete. Pilot 6 exposed the shared agent-map race under 32 concurrent trials. At least two trials created Harbor's built-in `OracleAgent` before the custom environment module changed the map. They failed while looking for a benchmark solution script that is not part of these coding tasks. Other trials used `BashAgent`, which confirms inconsistent agent selection in one rollout batch. The pilot was stopped before an optimizer update because it could not produce qualifying evidence. The incident is recorded in #9533. Artifact `2026.09.29.7` completed with fingerprint `df51bbcb` and pins MarinSkyRL `e26273f79`. Smoke 7 training succeeded at `/rav/snowball-python-expert-shellbox-smoke-7-coord/users-rav-checkpoints-snowball-python-expert-smoke-2026.09.29.7-177c6b868483`: all five H100×8 tasks completed without a failure or retry. Observed rollout batches completed 4/4, worker logs showed Shellbox's unsupported-tool recovery, and the full run had no `OracleAgent` or missing `solution/solve.sh` failure. The run completed one optimizer update and checkpoint. Its four-node HF export also succeeded without a failure or retry. Replacement pilot 7 training succeeded at `/rav/snowball-python-expert-pilot-7-coord/users-rav-checkpoints-snowball-python-expert-pilot-2026.09.29.7-aeecd23c5caa`. All five H100×8 tasks completed on their first attempt. The run completed four updates, its `global_step_4` checkpoint, and two post-update development passes. Train pass@1 reward was 7.42%, 7.42%, 7.03%, and 7.03% across the four updates; train pass@4 was 15.62%, 20.31%, 17.19%, and 20.31%. The fixed 300-problem development pass@1 was 7.0% before training and 6.0% after training, a decline of 1 percentage point. This candidate fails the positive-development gate. Its four-node HF export succeeded on the first attempt. The exported policy is `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/rav/checkpoints/snowball-python-expert-pilot/2026.09.29.7/exports/global_step_4/policy`. The export is the durable canonical policy; only the resumable Megatron storage has a seven-day lifetime. Keep the sealed final set closed and do not start MOPD acceptance for this checkpoint. Public code and collateral characterization completed at `/rav/snowball-python-expert-pilot-7-full-eval-coord`. Matched collateral evaluation is complete. MATH-500 accuracy decreased from 49.0% for the frozen parent to 45.2% for the pilot, a decline of 3.8 percentage points. IFBench strict prompt accuracy was 20.33% for both models. Loose prompt accuracy changed from 24.67% to 24.33%; strict instruction accuracy changed from 23.00% to 23.17%; and loose instruction accuracy changed from 26.67% to 26.83%. Each result contains 500 MATH-500 samples or 300 IFBench prompts. Matched public code evaluation is complete. The table uses the parent and candidate from the same graph. Intervals are normal 95% intervals over paired per-problem score differences. Every interval includes zero. | Benchmark | Samples | Frozen parent | Pilot | Change | Paired 95% interval | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | HumanEval+ | 164 | 42.07% | 50.61% | +8.54 points | -1.83 to +18.90 points | | MBPP+ | 378 | 44.18% | 44.18% | 0.00 points | -6.27 to +6.27 points | | CRUXEval input | 800 | 4.00% | 4.50% | +0.50 point | -1.46 to +2.46 points | | CRUXEval output | 800 | 7.63% | 8.38% | +0.75 point | -1.87 to +3.37 points | The first and matched frozen-parent runs have equal artifact model configs and the same evaluation seed, but HumanEval+ changed from 51.83% to 42.07%. Issue #9558 records this repeatability fault. The temporary workaround is to use only the matched pair and its paired intervals. The higher HumanEval+ point estimate is unresolved and does not override the negative development result. ## What happened ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Pinned Snowball SFT parent"] --> B["Audit 5,567 executable Python problems"] B --> C["Split by problem family
2,400 train / 300 development / 300 sealed final"] C --> D["Harbor tasks
Shellbox BashAgent + ShellSim + hidden tests"] D --> E["Smoke gates
Fix memory, runtime, agent, timeout, and tool-call faults"] E --> F["Four-update GRPO pilot
1,024 rollouts / 74 passed"] F --> G{"Did development pass@1 improve?"} G -->|"No: 7% to 6%"| H["Reject the checkpoint as a coding expert"] F --> I["Durable 79-shard Hugging Face export"] H --> J["Matched public and collateral characterization"] J --> K["Public code: mixed point changes
All paired intervals include zero"] J --> L["MATH-500: 49.0% to 45.2%
IFBench strict prompt: unchanged"] H --> M["Keep the sealed final set closed"] H --> N["Do not start teacher or MOPD acceptance"] ``` The training and export system worked. The capability gate failed because the development score decreased. Only 74 of 1,024 training rollouts passed their tests, so most prompt groups supplied no positive reward. The public-code point changes did not establish a stable gain, and MATH-500 decreased. | Day | Planned work | Required output | | --- | --- | --- | | 1 — Sep 29 | Pin inputs and runtime. Audit the source. Measure the frozen parent. Confirm reward diversity and runtime faults. | Source audit, parent aggregate scores, direct-smoke evidence, and linked fault reports. | | 2 — Sep 30 | Build the selected runtime with unsupported-tool recovery. Repeat the one-update smoke and reload its export through vLLM. Validate private-test isolation and known-pass, known-fail, and timeout canaries. | Reviewable spike PR, valid Shellbox traces, checkpoint, HF export, and reload. | | 3 — Oct 1 | Run bounded coding RL. Apply verified SFT first only if the pilot requires it. Evaluate intermediate checkpoints. | Candidate with a development-set gain, or a documented negative result. | | 4 — Oct 2 | Run matched public code and collateral characterization. Keep the sealed final set closed after the failed gate. | Negative candidate artifact with provenance, public scores, and limitations. | | 5 — Oct 3 | Preserve the export and close the report. Do not start teacher or MOPD acceptance for the rejected checkpoint. | Reproducible PR, run links, compute use, faults, and final decision. | Pilot 7 failed the development gate on September 29. The revised plan stops before the sealed-final and MOPD stages. Complete its export, run public code and collateral evaluations against the frozen parent, preserve the negative artifact, and close the spike with the measured result and follow-up options. The schedule assumes accelerator access. The first five-node layout used 40 H100s and failed from policy-plus-reference memory pressure. The Shellbox layout removes the unused KL reference and uses four policy nodes plus one rollout node. Smoke 4 proved that this 40-H100 layout initializes, but it failed at the agent request boundary before generation. Existing MOPD geometries suggest 48 H100s for single-teacher OPD and 64 for three-teacher MOPD. Revalidate each allocation for the selected checkpoint and runtime. The published SFT export reports FP32 tensors, so validate BF16 conversion and serving explicitly. Smoke 5 used about 12.7 H100-hours for training and 7.5 H100-hours for export, based on the observed 19-minute and 14-minute task durations. Smoke 6 matched those durations. Pilot 7 used 50.8 H100-hours for its 76-minute five-node training job and 7.0 H100-hours for its 13-minute four-node export, or 57.8 H100-hours in total. Keep large model artifacts in the same storage region. Completion criteria: - [x] Pin parent, tokenizer, data, runtime, verifier, and evaluation settings. - [x] Register separate training, development, and final problem sets with overlap checks. - [x] Complete a real update, checkpoint, HF export, and reload on the selected runtime. - [x] Report coding results and non-coding changes against the same frozen parent. - [x] Preserve the evaluated candidate and its provenance beyond temporary checkpoint expiry, including negative results. - [x] Apply the teacher and MOPD gate. issues.author: ravwojdyla-agent
issues.body:
`shellbox.agent:BashAgent` sends Harbor's provider-qualified model name directly to the SkyRL OpenAI endpoint. Harbor supplies `hosted_vllm/<served-name>`, but the endpoint accepts `<served-name>`. The endpoint returns HTTP 400 before generation.

The Snowball coding-expert smoke in #9528 confirmed this on 40 H100s. Every observed four-sample batch completed with 0/4 successful trajectories and `HTTPStatusError: 400 Bad Request`. The run used MarinSkyRL `92fbe512` and Shellbox `c96bf413`.

The path is deterministic:

1. The MarinSkyRL Harbor runner creates `model_name="hosted_vllm/<served-name>"`.
2. Harbor `BaseAgent` keeps that value as `model_alias`.
3. `BashAgent.run()` sends `model_alias` as the JSON `model` field.
4. The SkyRL HTTP bridge compares it with the vLLM served name and rejects it.

LiteLLM agents remove the provider prefix before they send the request. `BashAgent` owns its HTTP loop and does not perform that step.

Normalize Harbor's `hosted_vllm/` provider form before a direct OpenAI request. Preserve model names that do not use that provider form. Include the response body in request failure details so a future endpoint rejection is diagnosable.

The temporary workaround for #9528 strips the known prefix in `BashAgent` before the request. A focused test must cover the exact payload sent to the endpoint.

---

# Research

`BashAgent.run()` uses Harbor's `model_alias` directly in the OpenAI request. Harbor's `hosted_vllm/<served-name>` alias therefore reaches an endpoint that accepts only `<served-name>`, and `raise_for_status()` hides the response body from the error message. issues.author: yonromai
issues.body:
## TL;DR

- **Decision:** Should an Iris Kubernetes job be able to require one specific NVLink rack?
- **Need:** `group_by="nvlink.domain"` keeps a gang in one rack but does not choose which rack. A job limited to rack 392 needs to name it.
- **Current gap:** Iris skips that exact-rack constraint when building a Kubernetes Pod and lowercases the case-sensitive rack label before serialization.
- **Proposal:** [Draft PR #9478](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9478) would let a job require `nvlink.domain == "DH1-392-US-EAST-08A"`. The job could not run on another rack if the requested rack is missing or full.
- **Scope:** This feature would not reserve Hero training racks or prevent Batch jobs from using spare nodes there.

A read-only audit on September 26 found three Batch jobs using 24 GPUs on six other nodes in three of Hero's 11 training racks. It found no GPU double-booking and did not measure training harm. No placement with the changed controller has been tested live.

<details>
<summary>Evidence: placement audit, current code, and a local test failure</summary>

**Placement audit.** Iris controller `task_attempts` showed Hero using 16 nodes on each of 11 racks (176 four-GPU tasks). Racks 124, 125, and 129 each had 18 labeled nodes: 16 used by Hero and two by one Batch job. Captured Kubernetes node labels mapped the nodes to racks; FineLog `iris.profile` samples confirmed the Batch tasks ran there. The audit did not compare training speed with and without Batch work. A separate job requested only `group_by="nvlink.domain"`, so its placement did not test an exact-rack request.

**Actual rack label.** The captured Kubernetes node snapshot included `s1mwxs64` with `ds.coreweave.com/nvlink.domain=DH1-392-US-EAST-08A`. The uppercase characters matter for an exact label match.

**Current code.** [Gang topology](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/562d705673859548c58b46d8f2383ab8a053797f/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py#L285-L292) selects the `nvlink.domain` level without a rack value. The [Pod selector mapping](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/562d705673859548c58b46d8f2383ab8a053797f/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py#L179-L183) lists only `pool` and `region`; [unknown keys are skipped](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/562d705673859548c58b46d8f2383ab8a053797f/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py#L335-L346). [String constraints are lowercased](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/562d705673859548c58b46d8f2383ab8a053797f/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/constraints.py#L106-L110) before they are sent.

**Local reproduction.** Adding only the missing Pod mapping produced this failure for an illustrative uppercase rack label. It shows why the label's case must also survive serialization:

```text
assert manifest["spec"]["nodeSelector"]["ds.coreweave.com/nvlink.domain"] == rack
E AssertionError: assert 'dh1-001-us-east-08a' == 'DH1-001-US-EAST-08A'
```

The [draft PR's regression test](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/a30e700ae2cc164e28b8f244a8fe9a65f8584454/lib/iris/tests/cluster/backends/k8s/test_pod_manifest.py#L681-L693) checks that the exact label survives controller storage and reaches the Pod's selector and required affinity.

</details>

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

`group_by="nvlink.domain"` keeps a gang in one NVLink domain but cannot name the rack; the Kubernetes backend renders only `pool` and `region` constraints as node selectors. `AttributeValue` lowercases strings, so the current constraint round trip loses the case of CoreWeave rack labels. A [prior rack-pinning incident](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/425) required temporary `iris.pool` labels to keep builds on an authorized rack.

**Relevant code**
- [`coreweave_topology.py#L58-L76`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/coreweave_topology.py#L58-L76) — gang topology levels
- [`constraints.py#L92-L103`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/constraints.py#L92-L103) — string normalization
- [`tasks.py#L154-L157`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py#L154-L157) — supported node selectors

# Proposed Fix

I recommend supporting an opt-in, required `nvlink.domain == <rack label>` constraint that preserves the label's case and adds both a Pod selector and required node affinity. [Kueue writes its assigned topology label into the selector](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/blob/main/pkg/controller/tas/topology_ungater.go#L1888-L1902), and [Kubernetes requires selector and affinity together](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/assign-pod-node/#node-affinity), so the affinity retains the named-rack requirement after admission. [Draft PR #9478](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9478) implements this scope; review and a live placement check belong there. A missing or full rack leaves the job pending, and this constraint does not reserve training racks or resolve the Batch contention in [#8925](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8925).

comments.author: RavnaBergsndot
comments.body:
In latentMoE, we can try initializing the up/down projections as semi-orthogonal matrices and either:

A: using an orthogonality-preserving optimizer such as the one introduced in https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06218 to update them
or
B: freezing them, keeping them semi-orthogonal and not updating them at all, while relying the rest of the NN to adapt

Rationale: up/down projections in latentMoE are themselves small, shared by all experts of the same layer, therefore not really having the capability to do meaningful computation for the whole NN. We should see them as information-preserving maps instead, and worry more about gradient pathology/distortion, rather than the potential loss of the degree of freedom/expressivity by using semi-orthogonal matrices.
Also if we take the "no meaningful computation" hypothesis really seriously, option B should only have negligible performance degradation compared to A. And if we use B, no new optimizer and no new hyperparameter tuning are needed.

issues.author: dlwh
issues.body:
## TL;DR

The full GraphWalks evaluation of `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21` scored F1 0.060072 on 920 examples. Sample inspection found that 859 responses (93.4%) failed the final-answer parser, and every one reached the request's roughly 4,100-token output limit. Many end mid-reasoning or mid-edge-list. The scored result is dominated by generation truncation. A larger output budget has not yet been tested.

## Description

GraphWalks has 1,150 examples. At the 262,144-token serving cap, Grug scored 920 and skipped 230 for context. `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` scored F1 0.516097 on 750 examples and skipped 400 for context. On the 750 examples both models scored, Grug's F1 was 0.073689 and Qwen's was 0.516097.

The evaluator sets each request's `max_tokens` to `max(4096, tokenized gold answer length + 4096)` and requires a `Final Answer: [...]` on the response's last line. The archive contains the raw outputs, parsed lists, gold lists, and grades. The jobs succeeded and wrote their records. [PR #9511](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9511) adds the evaluator and records run provenance.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Test whether a larger generation budget lets the models finish their reasoning and produce final answers, especially for the long prompts. Record the server's `finish_reason` and compare on the same examples. Then assess any remaining task or parsing errors separately.

## Status

- Grug: F1 0.060072; benchmark 1,150; scored 920; context skips 230; output-cap selection skips 0; request errors 0. Only 61/920 outputs were parseable. Their mean F1 was 0.906011, conditional on producing a final answer.
- Qwen: F1 0.516097; scored 750; context skips 400; output-cap selection skips 0; request errors 0. 395/750 outputs were parseable. Their mean F1 was 0.979930, conditional on producing a final answer.
- For Grug, all 859 unparseable outputs were within three retokenized tokens of their requested generation budget or longer; the median was one token below it. For Qwen, all 355 unparseable outputs were at or above that budget after retokenization. This strongly indicates truncation, but the evaluator did not store `finish_reason`.
- A more permissive search for a completed `Final Answer: [...]` anywhere in the response found 62 additional candidates in each run. Many Grug matches came from quoted instructions or earlier reasoning. A parser change alone cannot explain its low score.
- A controlled larger-budget run has not been submitted.

## Links

- Implementation and run notes: [PR #9511](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9511)
- Grug record: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/20260929-163239-grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft-262k-2026-09-21-graphwalks-a353/record.json`
- Qwen record: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/20260929-163929-qwen3.6-35b-a3b-graphwalks-917b/record.json`

## Decision Log

- Use the models' 262,144-token serving cap; report context skips separately from scored examples.
- Keep the reported F1 tied to the original 4,096-token minimum output policy. Do not reinterpret parsed-only F1 as full-run performance.

## Conclusion

The saved outputs identify generation truncation as the main reason most responses received zero. The model's accuracy with enough output tokens remains unmeasured. A bounded larger-budget probe should precede another full run.

🤖 I read the sealed FineStore `samples` tables for both full runs and retokenized each saved response with its model tokenizer. Representative saved Grug outputs:

For our graph, the order is cfcd208495, c81e728d9d, eccbc87e4b, a87ff679a2”. It has no final-answer line. Retokenized response: 4,134 tokens; request budget: 4,135.

issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
Generate realistic computational biology tasks for **Harbor**, with **deterministic executable rewards and no LLM-as-a-judge**. Deliver public, reusable task packages that others can plug into their pipelines.

Development starts from the [BioTasks integration branch, `codex/bio-tasks`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/codex/bio-tasks). Create a separate `codex/bio-tasks-<area>` feature branch and worktree for each workstream, and open draft pull requests with `codex/bio-tasks` as the base. Integrate changes through reviewed pull requests; keep `main` unchanged during this phase.

The [canonical plan](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-tasks/docs/experiments/bio-task-generation/index.md) defines the future pipeline. It is under review; task authoring is paused while we specify the process. Earlier prototypes and validation evidence remain linked from the plan and are not a completed dataset release.

- Discover useful workflows from tools, reusable pipelines, tutorials and paper-analysis repositories, with no repository-count cutoff. Benchmarks are optional inspiration; preserve existing OOD exclusions.
- Use observed biological data as the corpus backbone, with labeled adaptations and simulations. Include focused analyses and connected workflows; add variants for meaningful scientific work.
- Require CPU-only Daytona execution, explicit resources, native-package reference solutions and independently checked artifact grading. Aim for most solves to take 2–10 minutes, with a longer-running tail; 30 minutes is a heuristic, not a hard ceiling.
- Version the discover, inspect, propose, build and challenge prompts. Validate environments, references, grader repeatability, incorrect submissions and initial independent trial solves before scaling.
- Publish code, eligible inputs, references, graders and validation evidence. Keep oracle answers outside solver-visible inputs. Public Hugging Face distribution is proposed; the release repository is not yet selected.

Detailed plan: [discovery](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-tasks/docs/experiments/bio-task-generation/discovery.md), [authoring](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-tasks/docs/experiments/bio-task-generation/task-authoring.md), [requirements](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-tasks/docs/experiments/bio-task-generation/requirements.md), [validation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-tasks/docs/experiments/bio-task-generation/validation.md), [storage](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-tasks/docs/experiments/bio-task-generation/storage.md), and [transcriptomics examples](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/bio-tasks/docs/experiments/bio-task-generation/examples/transcriptomics.md).

Next: review a focused transcriptomics task and a connected analysis, then broaden the candidate portfolio. Data splitting, downstream model training, teacher-trace collection and inference configuration are outside this issue.

All pilot and diagnostic Iris jobs are terminal; no further GPU jobs are planned for this model. The new corpus, training recipe, and hardware are still pending. Leave the native and HF model artifacts under the managed `tmp/ttl=14d/` lifecycle prefix; no manual deletion is planned. This status closes the present pilot attempt while preserving its ungraded result and reproducibility links below.

- **Trajectory review (September 24):** The read-only one-CPU job `/exedev/bio-bix51-postsft-trajectory-lite-20260924-204812` succeeded and checked the archived trajectory SHA256 `b5508f2d61e99bc68703c1b5f92cfbc01a6e13631dd05d5026a061a3e64c3073`. The graded pre-SFT student did submit a wrong answer (73.5366) after recovering from three parse errors; this is one attempt per checkpoint. The trajectory is archived with SHA256 `b5508f2d61e99bc68703c1b5f92cfbc01a6e13631dd05d5026a061a3e64c3073`. A separate fixed-prompt response failed JSON parsing under a 512-token cap; its finish reason was not recorded, so it cannot isolate a model or harness cause. The subsequent trajectory review and closure decision are recorded above. Both Iris jobs are terminal; no further GPU run was submitted.

- **Native checkpoint succeeded; separate HF export stopped at startup (September 24, 19:18 UTC):** Iris job `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-cosine10-native-20260924-190343` completed all ten updates on the same pinned student, 31 traces, and cosine recipe. - **Ten updates completed; final export timed out (September 24, 18:47 UTC):** Iris job `/exedev/bio-logistic-sft-cosine10-finitegate-20260924-173026` ran the approved 31 accepted traces, 10 cosine steps, batch 8, length 4,096, native Snowball loss with the CPU-tested layout fix, and 32 H100s. All ten optimizer updates logged finite losses. Fixed training-batch loss was 0.753316 before training, spiked to 3.830647 after update 1, and reached 0.206134 after update 10. The standard Levanter 39-shard BF16 HF export began, but slowed substantially: the last verified rank-zero progress was 114/134 GB and entering shard 34/39 at 18:45 UTC. Iris then reported `Execution timeout exceeded`; all four tasks are terminal. The run has **no verified final index or `training-complete.json` marker**, so the partial export at `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=14d/bio-sft/bio-logistic-sft-sep21-cosine10-finitegate-20260924/` must not be served. Thread snapshots placed ranks in that gather/barrier path, but do not establish why this run took longer than the earlier export. - The recommendation is now September 21 with explicit `/nothink`, followed by a complete unchanged `bix-51-q2` attempt before SFT. The earlier default-thinking failure does not justify preferring September 16. The later full-task baseline above establishes September 21 with `/nothink` as the current candidate; no biology SFT has run. Requests, responses, parser, configuration and hashes are preserved at `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/snowball-sep21-bix51-smoke-20260922-195017/results/diagnostics/nothink-20260922/`; the original interrupted trial and its null grade remain unchanged.

- Family: `cohort-logistic-aic-v1`, modeled on `bix-51-q2`: fit an unpenalized logistic regression with an intercept and BMI, then report AIC. The 32 fresh simulated cohorts use seed `20260921` and independently fitted reference answers. All siblings form one training split; the original benchmark task, data, answers, and teacher attempts are excluded from training.
- Teacher runs: [first attempt](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/bio-siblings-glm53-smoke-20260922-160257-teacher) and [remaining 31](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/bio-siblings-glm53-batch31-20260922-161619-teacher). One attempt per task, no trial retries or summarization. These are synthetic-data results, not a BixBench score.
- Raw run artifacts live under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/<run-id>/results/`. The batch run's `provenance/_bio_tasks.zip` preserves all 32 packaged Harbor tasks; its other provenance files preserve the launch plan and executed runner/export code.
- Curated corpus: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/bio-siblings-glm53-batch31-20260922-161619-teacher/results/training-corpus/`. It contains `manifest.json`, all 32 attempts in `ledger.jsonl`, review decisions, 31 accepted `conversations.jsonl` records, Harmony/rendered exports, and the audit source. `conversations.jsonl` SHA256: `31925a115e5d98495705842c17725233bdef234a21d2761ef1e0d3117af1fc5a`.
- Limitation: task `00007` reversed the requested response labels. AIC is invariant to that reversal, so the numerical reward remains 1 while the trace is excluded from SFT. This shortcut needs attention before using the family for RL. This one-family pilot does not establish broad biological coverage.
- SFT preparation: all 31 conversations passed the native loader with assistant-only loss, a 4,096-token limit, no packing, and no validation split. The eight-H100 initialized-weight memory test passed; next validate the pinned checkpoint import/export, train on the accepted traces, and evaluate the unchanged original task under a matched protocol. No expert-freezing or LoRA method has been selected.

- Eight-H100 memory test: two optimizer updates completed on the full 67B architecture with initialized weights and synthetic tokens. Configuration: [PR #9316 at `9394f2c`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/9394f2cd2b6c1b2154dd26c69e230df715fcaf99), 8×H100 80GB, 64 CPU cores / 768 GiB host RAM, one JAX process, BF16 parameters, demo MuonH/Adam optimizer, optimizer-state host offloading, context sharding across 8 devices, batch 8, sequence length 4,096, and `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.9`. Iris job `/exedev/bio-grug-eight-h100-probe-20260922-182903` and task both succeeded; logs confirm 2/2 updates. Execution took 218.9 seconds and peak JAX allocator use was 67,653,347,256 bytes (63.01 GiB) per GPU. This excludes allocations outside JAX and does not establish checkpoint-specific SFT quality. No pretrained weights were downloaded and no checkpoints were written. The GPUs are released.

- Reproducibility and data check: the corpus now also contains `grug-ready-20260922/generator-source.zip`, `gpu-probe-source.zip`, `data-preflight.py`, and `data-preflight.json`. The generator source matches the original task-manifest hashes. CPU job `/exedev/bio-grug-data-preflight-20260922-184716` succeeded against the candidate training backend: all 31 conversations retained exact assistant-only loss weights over 256 presentations (8 or 9 per conversation, 222,695 supervised tokens), with no packing or validation split. The GPU probe used synthetic tokens; a pretrained run with these conversations remains pending.

- Existing checkpoint found (September 22): the exact pinned revision is present on CoreWeave US-EAST-02A node `g83b4e8` at `/hf/cache/models--open-athena--Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.16/snapshots/ad02eb6b1e35759e1cfeac17ec369fe5a48651ff`. Its index references 39 shards, all present, totaling 134,157,827,064 bytes. This was a metadata check; payloads have not been rehashed. The original export also remains at `gs://marin-us-central2/users/held/grug_sft/grug-67b-sft-20260914-semantic-1000/exports/step-158000/hf-bf16`; its `hf_upload_complete.json` identifies the pinned repository and revision and records all 39 shard SHA256 values. The successful `/held/grug-semantic-sft-158000-upload-hf` log independently confirms that revision. The earlier missing-shard report covered only the partial regional S3 mirror. No weights were downloaded or moved during this search, and no GPUs were allocated. Reusing the node cache for our training worker still needs placement or regional staging; external downloads remain disabled.

- Regional staging status: 34/39 September 16 shards are now present in the existing US-EAST-02A mirror. The newly copied shards were checked against the original SHA256 receipt before transfer. Shard 35's transfer timed out; its owned subprocess was stopped and verified absent. Five shards (17,080,453,656 bytes) and metadata finalization remain. No completion marker has been written, no external model downloads occurred, and biology SFT has not started.

- Checkpoint reconsideration: the [September 21 release](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21) changes special-token initialization and learning rates. Its [EvalDash results](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/models/open-athena-Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21), checked September 22, include latest completed MATH500 accuracy 0.706 (500 items) and MBPP+ pass@1 0.531746 (378 items). These are not a matched September 16 comparison or a BixBench result. The default-thinking readiness test below failed; the later `/nothink` diagnostic at the top changes the recommendation. The 31 source conversations remain reusable.

- September 21 readiness check: the newer checkpoint still failed the Terminus output format on `bix-51-q2`. All 191 saved agent responses received parsing-error feedback and no commands executed. The run was stopped after 642 seconds, before the configured one-hour agent limit, and remains ungraded; this does not measure biological task accuracy. All eight GPUs and the owned Daytona sandbox are released. One attempt, no trial retries, unchanged task files and grader, native inference template with default thinking, Terminus-2, 32,768 input / 8,192 output tokens. Used the complete existing US-EAST-02A mirror at HF revision `a23aa7bbc864a73970a3dd9e499168c45d37f497`; the stored transfer receipt agrees with all 39 published shard hashes. Revision `b8c07f7df1df65525abbfdbcd1572318ba11c42f` changes documentation only. No external weights were downloaded. Harbor `d072bef08e54050880b484eb81d892944d1d82fb`, Marin `12bbd5d45b1b176167ab3cfe905e06004c2f02e3`, vLLM `f0d7cc7f587482e0ab771e3c9715e726eb914e60`.

- The model repeatedly emitted native `<tool_call>` wrappers containing a single command object rather than the requested Terminus `analysis`, `plan`, and `commands` object. The instructions included the expected schema. This supports a format mismatch; it does not establish a harness bug or a controlled September 16 versus September 21 comparison. Run `snowball-sep21-bix51-smoke-20260922-195017` is preserved at `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/snowball-sep21-bix51-smoke-20260922-195017/`, including `record.json`, native results, episode logs, and `results/protocol-stop.json`. Trial `bix-51-q2__6guSjZw` has trajectory SHA256 `b0675111f8f099e90894d77f89da02a1750c516015801f3dacb4dbc80244791a`. The canonical record retains a null grade and explicitly records the operator stop.

- Checkpoint-conversion gate: an additional tiny model check at PR #9316 revision `9394f2cd2b6c1b2154dd26c69e230df715fcaf99` preserved all 103 tensors exactly through HF import, the trainer initializer, router-bias application, and HF export. Its CPU forward comparison against sliding attention failed (maximum absolute difference 0.00034105). A diagnostic matched exactly when both sides used full attention (maximum difference 0.0): the CPU reference ignores the scanned model’s precomputed FA4 window bounds. The original sliding-attention check remains failed; parity on the actual GPU attention path is still required before biology SFT. Jobs: `/exedev/bio-grug-format-check-20260922-195340` and `/exedev/bio-grug-format-diagnostic-20260922-195821`; both are terminal. No tolerance was relaxed or checkpoint weights altered.
