- [`train.py#L304`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe/train.py#L304) — `train_step`; consumes `GrugLmExample` batches via `DataLoader`/`AsyncDataset`
- [`model.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe/model.py) — `GrugModelConfig` / `Transformer`
- [`grug_moe.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py) + [`_moe/ep_deepep.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_deepep.py) — MoE dispatch / DeepEP GPU expert-parallel backend (the perf-critical path)

Related: #4312 (improve 8×H100 MoE MFU), #6695 (verify CE path in May profile), #6386 (CoreWeave Grug MoE canary scaling).

# Proposed approach (for review before I build it)
A single runnable script (e.g. `experiments/grug/moe/repro_gpu.py`) that:
1. Builds `GrugModelConfig` + the FSDP/expert-parallel mesh exactly as `launch_cw_scale.py` does (reuse `build_scale_model` and the `expert_axis`/`replica_axis` math), but imports **only** Levanter/Haliax/JAX — no `marin.execution`, no Fray/Iris, no executor.
2. Replaces the dataset with an in-process synthetic source yielding random-token `GrugLmExample` batches of the right `[batch, seq]` shape — zero I/O, no tokenize.
3. Runs N steps with the existing `train_step`, warms up past compile, and prints step time / tokens-per-sec / MFU, optionally a `jax_profile` window.

This keeps the perf-critical model + MoE EP code identical to production while removing every dependency an external engineer can't run.

**Decisions I need from you before implementing:**
1. **Target scale** — single 8×H100 node (~9.5B canary class, runs anywhere) or the full 90B/256-GPU multi-node shape? Standalone+shareable argues for single-node by default, multi-node opt-in via env.
2. **"Replicates the GPU performance"** — what's the acceptance metric? Match the real run's step time / MFU within some % at a fixed shape, or just "exercises the same kernels and reports throughput"?
3. **Dependency surface** — strictly Levanter+JAX (so it ships outside this repo), or is "no Marin executor / no Iris, but still inside the marin tree" good enough?

Tell me 1–3 (or just "single-node, throughput-only, inside the tree" and I'll run with it) and I'll open the PR.

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 Standalone GPU MoE repro — working, validated on a single 8×H100 node

Added [`experiments/grug/moe/standalone_repro.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/rav/grug-moe-standalone-6759/experiments/grug/moe/standalone_repro.py) on branch [`rav/grug-moe-standalone-6759`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/rav/grug-moe-standalone-6759) (off `main`). Single-file launcher that runs the production grug MoE train step on synthetic data with **no Marin infra** — no iris/fray dispatch, no GCS/R2 data, no W&B required. Just `python -m experiments.grug.moe.standalone_repro`.

**What it does**
- builds the May `d=2560` shape from `main`'s `GrugModelConfig` (fully CLI-configurable: `--hidden-dim/--num-layers/--num-experts/--top-k/--seq-len/--sliding-window/--moe-impl/--attn-impl/--remat`)
- deterministic in-memory token stream (`SyntheticGrugDataset`, ported from the `codex/deepep-*` branch) — zero data I/O, optional periodic EOS + packed `segment_ids`
- builds the compact `(replica_dcn, data, expert, model)` mesh and calls the in-process `_run_grug_local` directly (the same entry each Fray worker runs) — so it needs no dispatch layer
- mesh configurable; **defaults to 2×8×H100** (`--expert-axis 8`, replica = `jax.process_count()`)
- profiling: rank-0 xprof trace logged as a **W&B artifact** under `--wandb`; opt-in `--perfetto-trace` also bundles the perfetto trace (ui.perfetto.dev)

**Validated on 1×8×H100 (`cw-us-east-02a`)** — mirrors the codex single-node `GM2560-…-N1` shape (2 layers / 256 experts):
- run `GM2560-STANDALONE-L2-E8-B8-EOS512-N1-cw-20260701-001025` — finished 30/30 steps, fail=0
- 5.75B params (d2560, 2 layers, 256 experts top-4, seq 4096); E8M1 8-process multi-controller
- loss 1.43 → 1.12; **MFU ~5.5** (p50 5.52); **145K tok/s**; `ring` MoE + `gpu_fa4_cute` + `save_moe`
- xprof trace (steps 8–15) captured on rank 0 and logged as a W&B artifact
- the standalone auto-detected the Iris job context and initialized `jax.distributed` with **no code changes** (same `_run_grug_local` as production)

**Gotchas found running on the iris GPU path** (all worth documenting):
1. `gpu_fa4_cute` requires packed `segment_ids` — run synthetic data with `--eos-interval > 0`; a plain causal mask (`eos_interval=0`) is rejected with `NotImplementedError: … requires packed segment_ids`.
2. iris defaults `JAX_COMPILATION_CACHE_DIR` to `s3://…/compilation-cache`, and XLA's per-fusion autotune sub-cache has no `s3://` filesystem driver → `UNIMPLEMENTED: File system scheme 's3'`. Fix: pass a local `JAX_COMPILATION_CACHE_DIR` (iris respects an explicit setting). Only bites on the iris path, not an external box.
3. levanter's profiler wrote a perfetto trace on **every** rank and barriered across all ranks — the concurrent perfetto write corrupted/hung (`BadGzipFile`) at 8 ranks. Fixed by adding `create_perfetto_trace` + `profile_process_index` to `ProfilerConfig` (defaults preserve behavior): profile rank 0 only, keep the stop barrier on all ranks. The standalone profiles rank 0 with perfetto off by default.

MFU ~5.5 is expected for this smoke shape (batch 8 = 1/device, only 2 layers → overhead-dominated, `Adam` not `muonh`); scaling layers/batch or switching to muonh raises it. Full `d2560` (26 layers / 256 experts) won't fit one node — it was sized for 32.

Branch is pushed (`rav/grug-moe-standalone-6759`, 3 commits); PR against `main` next.

spillover_issues.author: rjpower
spillover_issues.body:
## Summary

Construct the output-path-dependent training config fields in `train_lm`'s `build_config(ctx)` instead of baking them into a blank config later, on the worker, at run time. Retire `bake_output_path` / `_update_config_to_use_out_path` and the separate `output_path` field threading. This is leftover from the old executor framework and is now pure indirection under the lazy `ArtifactStep` model.

## Current shape (config built blank, mutated later, on a different machine)

1. **Coordinator** — `train_lm`'s `build_config(ctx)` (`lib/marin/src/marin/experiment/train.py:131-171`) builds a `TrainLmOnPodConfig` whose inner `TrainLmConfig` has the checkpointer at its *default* base path, `hf_save_path=None`, and `trainer.id` possibly `None`. The real output dir is **not** baked in — it is carried alongside as a separate `output_path=ctx.output_path` field.
2. **Worker** — `run_levanter_train_lm` → `_prepare_training_run` (`lib/marin/src/marin/training/training.py:490-522`) then calls `_update_config_to_use_out_path` → `bake_output_path`, a cascade of `dataclasses.replace` that injects `checkpointer.base_path = <out>/checkpoints`, `temporary_base_path`, and `hf_save_path = <out>/hf`; plus `_enforce_run_id` imputing `trainer.id` from `basename(output_path)`, a cpu `require_accelerator` toggle, and `doublecheck_paths`.

So the config is *constructed* in one place and its path-dependent fields are *filled in* in another, on a different machine, at run time.

## Why it exists (and why it's now obsolete)

The docstring says it outright (`_update_config_to_use_out_path`, `training.py:258`): _"useful when running with the executor framework, where the output path is set by the executor."_ In the **old** executor model, steps were built at **import time**, before the executor assigned the content-hash output path (`name-<hash>`) — the path did not exist at construction, so it had to be baked in late, on the worker, right before launch.

Under the lazy model `build_config(ctx)` runs with `ctx.output_path` already resolved (`{prefix}/{name}/{version}`), so the config can be constructed correctly up front. Verified: `bake_output_path` is a **pure function of `(train_config, output_path)`** with no worker-side dependency — even the region-local temp goes through `marin_temp_bucket(source_prefix=output_path)` (`lib/rigging/src/rigging/filesystem.py:341`), which derives the region from the **output path**, not the worker VM region. Run-id imputation is just `basename(output_path)`, and the cpu toggle depends only on `resources` — both build-time-knowable.

## Proposed change

- Build the full `TrainerConfig` in `build_config(ctx)` with the real `checkpointer.base_path`, `temporary_base_path`, `hf_save_path` (see #6752 re: dropping the forced HF path), and `trainer.id` — directly from `ctx.output_path`.
- Keep on the worker only what is genuinely run-time:
  - `resolve_training_env` — assembling env vars (GIT_COMMIT, WANDB, JAX compilation-cache dir, accel defaults) and applying them to `os.environ` for levanter;
  - `doublecheck_paths` — the runtime check that configured GCS paths match the live VM region.
- Delete `bake_output_path`, `_update_config_to_use_out_path`, the separate `output_path` field threading, and the run-id-from-output-path imputation; replace "build blank, mutate later" with "build it right once."

## Relationship to #6752

#6752 (HF export as a separate `export_hf` step) wants HF export out of `bake_output_path` anyway. This cleanup naturally removes the forced `hf_save_path` assignment; coordinate the two so the HF path is dropped here and re-introduced as its own step there.

## Blast radius

`_prepare_training_run` is shared by LM **and** DPO (`run_levanter_train_lm` / `run_levanter_train_dpo`) and feeds many experiments; `bake_output_path` / `impute_run_id` are also used by other call sites. This is a real refactor of the shared training entry, not a drop-in — it was not required to make the new steps *run*, only to make them clean.

## Key references

- `lib/marin/src/marin/training/training.py:176-200` — `bake_output_path`
- `lib/marin/src/marin/training/training.py:249-272` — `_update_config_to_use_out_path` (docstring naming the executor-framework origin at `:258`)
- `lib/marin/src/marin/training/training.py:203-246` — `impute_run_id` / `:403` `_enforce_run_id`
- `lib/marin/src/marin/training/training.py:490-522` — `_prepare_training_run` (shared LM/DPO)
- `lib/marin/src/marin/experiment/train.py:131-171` — `build_config` that already has `ctx.output_path`
- `lib/rigging/src/rigging/filesystem.py:341` — `marin_temp_bucket(source_prefix=...)` (region from output path, not VM)

_Filed from the lazy ArtifactStep / executor-context adoption work; surfaced while reviewing the training config path._

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read issue + duplicate-work preflight
- [x] Verify technical claims against the code
- [x] Post analysis (no PR — large refactor on unmerged code)

# Research

Proposal is **sound and verified**, but this is a refactor of the shared LM/DPO training entry (>100 lines, the issue says so itself), and — critically — **the code it targets does not exist on `main`.** `experiment/train.py`, `build_config(ctx)`, and `ctx.output_path` live only in the branch of #6649 ([`weaver/adopt-executor-context-for-remai`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/6649), still OPEN). The issue's line refs match that branch exactly (`build_config` at `train.py:131`, `bake_output_path` at `training.py:176`, `_update_config_to_use_out_path` at `:249`). So this is **stacked-on-#6649 cleanup**, not a `main` change. Per scope rules I'm posting analysis rather than a PR.

Claims I confirmed:
- `bake_output_path` **is** a pure fn of `(train_config, output_path)` — no worker/VM dependency (`training.py:176-200`, branch).
- Region-local temp comes from the **output path**, not the VM: `marin_temp_bucket(source_prefix=...)` — *"An explicit source_prefix fully determines the backend and region"* ([`filesystem.py:378-385`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/rigging/src/rigging/filesystem.py#L378-L385)).
- Run-id imputation case 4 is `basename(output_path)`; cpu `require_accelerator` toggle depends only on `resources`, which `build_config` already has via `ctx.runtime_arg("train_resources")` (`train.py:168`). Both build-time-knowable. ✔

# Proposed approach (for #6649 author)

The build-time / run-time split the issue describes is correct. **Build-time** (move into `build_config(ctx)`): `bake_output_path` (base_path, temporary_base_path, hf_save_path), run-id, cpu toggle, `_maybe_override_auto_build_caches`. **Run-time, keep on worker**: `resolve_training_env` (GIT_COMMIT/WANDB/JAX cache — its `marin_temp_bucket` call has **no** `source_prefix`, so it's genuinely launcher/region-dependent, `training.py:480-484`) and `doublecheck_paths` (live VM-region check).

Three nuances the "it's just `bake_output_path` + run-id" framing misses — handle these in the move, don't drop them:

1. **Adapter/PEFT path rewrite.** `_update_config_to_use_out_path` also nulls `hf_save_path` and sets `peft_save_path` for adapter LM/DPO (`training.py:265-270`, branch). Pure, so it moves to `build_config` too — but it must move *with* the hf-path logic, and this is exactly the seam #6752 (separate `export_hf` step) wants to cut. Coordinate: drop the forced `hf_save_path` here, reintroduce as its own step there.
2. **Run-id precedence changes.** `impute_run_id` priority is `trainer.id` → `env_vars["RUN_ID"]` → `os.environ["RUN_ID"]` → `basename(output_path)` (`training.py:203-246`). `build_config` already passes `id=run_id` (`train.py:138`), so build-time imputation is usually a no-op — but moving it build-time means a worker-side `RUN_ID` **env var no longer overrides**. Confirm nothing relies on that (Iris/ferry-injected `RUN_ID`).
3. **DPO auto-schedule reads tokenizer stats.** `_maybe_auto_resolve_dpo_schedule` → `_dpo_training_dataset_size` does I/O (`training.py:303-305`). Decide explicitly whether it stays worker-side or moves; it is *not* a pure config transform like the rest.

Net: `_prepare_training_run` shrinks to `resolve_training_env` + `_apply_env_to_process` + `doublecheck_paths`; `bake_output_path` / `_update_config_to_use_out_path` / `_enforce_run_id` / the separate `output_path` field thread get deleted. Land it as a follow-up commit on #6649 (or a PR stacked on it), gated on the #6752 hf-export decision.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body:
🤖 Revisited now that the lazy ArtifactStep work (#6649) has landed. Opened #6809 for the cleanup, but with a correction to this issue's proposed mechanism.

**The cleaner way already exists in-tree.** The grug base/moe launchers build their checkpointer paths directly from `output_path` and never touch `bake_output_path`. `train_lm` was the last holdout on the blank-config-then-`dataclasses.replace`-cascade. So the fix is to make `train_lm` match grug and delete the cascade — no new machinery.

**But building the paths inside `build_config(ctx)` (as this issue proposes) is subtly wrong.** `build_config` runs at *fingerprint* time too, with `ctx.output_path == "<output_path>"`. Two consequences the earlier analysis missed:

1. **Region leak into identity.** `temporary_checkpoint_base_path("<output_path>")` → `marin_temp_bucket` can't parse a region from the placeholder, so it falls through to `marin_prefix()` and bakes the *ambient cluster's root* into the fingerprint. Identity would then depend on which cluster you lowered from. (The earlier comment's claim that the temp path is "build-time-knowable and pure" holds for the VM, but not for the fingerprint placeholder.)
2. **Fingerprint churn.** Moving `base_path` into `build_config` changes the fingerprinted value from the default `"checkpoints/"` to `"<output_path>/checkpoints"` — a new hash for every existing train artifact, forcing TPU recompute of cached fixed-version runs.

Grug sidesteps both by keeping path construction in its `run` callable (real `output_path`, after fingerprinting). #6809 does the same for `train_lm`: it deletes `bake_output_path` / `_update_config_to_use_out_path` / `impute_run_id` / `_enforce_run_id` and replaces them with direct construction (`resolve_checkpointer_output_path` + `apply_output_path` + `_resolve_run_id`, the first now shared with grug), while leaving the fingerprint byte-for-byte unchanged.

Scope notes: DPO isn't wired into the lazy layer yet (no `TrainDpoOnPodConfig` constructor in production), so `_prepare_training_run` is shared but only `train_lm` exercised the cascade. The forced `hf_save_path` is preserved for now — dropping it belongs with #6752's separate `export_hf` step, not this structural cleanup.

spillover_issues.author: dlwh
spillover_issues.body:
## Candidate-9 result (2026-09-29): sweep complete

The matched candidate-9 test records no final pure-EMA Paloma win over its same-seed controls at d512 or d768. Mean losses are:

| Arm | d512 | d768 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Control | 2.98053 | 2.72219 |
| Standard α=1 | 2.99639 (+0.01586) | 2.73433 (+0.01214) |
| α=1, coda warmup | 2.99379 (+0.01325) | 2.73282 (+0.01063), seed0 repeat |
| α=1, preserve bigram selection | 2.98831 (+0.00777) | 2.72487 (+0.00268) |

Parentheses give loss minus the matched control; lower is better. Preservation recovers most of standard α=1's penalty at both widths but remains worse on both seeds; it is a persistent source-selection change with unchanged parameter shapes. Recorded midpoint/final evaluations and sampled late training windows do not show the hypothesized late win. These runs modify the inherited candidate-9 recipe; no full BO-specific hyperparameter search or dense-Transformer replication was performed. Pause this line after the authorized sweep; no further runs are planned. [Final seed-paired results, learning windows, throughput and provenance](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9280#issuecomment-5901009948).

The one authorized unchanged d768 warmup seed0 repeat completed all 7325 updates and evaluations on Iris/W&B. It passed the original NaN step 5441 with finite loss and finished at Paloma 2.73488. This shows nonrecurrence in one attempt; the original failure cause remains unknown. Its paired mean uses the successful repeat with original seed1 and is conditioned on completion. Original d768 α=.707 seed0 failed at 1532 and was not retried; seed1 finished at 2.73111, so no two-seed final mean exists for that arm. Standard d512 α=1 seed0 completed training/evaluation, then failed during tracker shutdown; its primary score is saved and blend scores are unavailable. All authorized attempts are now terminal and the monitor is stopped. [Failures](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9280#issuecomment-5899790837), [repeat authorization and recipe](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9280#issuecomment-5899890438).

Earlier May-ladder loss wins below remain confounded by attention-window semantics. [d512 detailed results](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9280#issuecomment-5899525010), [standard d768](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9280#issuecomment-5900079796), [preservation d768](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9280#issuecomment-5900468443).

## Goal

Test the boundary operator from [arXiv 2609.19107](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19107) ("How Model Growth, Recursion, and Boundary Operators Influence Scaling Exponents") on the grug MoE block, at matched parameters and FLOPs, before building any of the paper's looping/growth machinery.

The operator (paper's Operator-1, K=1, no looping, no growth): split the layers into prelude/core/coda (as even as possible; remainders to core first, then coda). The core starts from `h₀ = 0`, so its entry state is `BO(0, e) = α·e` where `e` is the prelude's output; after the last core block, the coda's entry state is `BO(h, e) = rms_norm(h) + α·e`. One RMSNorm and two vector-adds; zero new parameters.

Why this first: the paper reports the operator alone (no recursion, no growth) already moves the scaling exponent — effective compute multiplier ≈1.25× at 1e20 FLOPs. It is the cheapest decisive test of whether the paper's axes transfer to the MoE template: if the operator doesn't move the grug isoflop curves, looping/growth almost certainly won't either.

## Plan

- Variant `experiments/grug/moe_boundary/` copied from `experiments/grug/moe/` (copy-first per the grug archive workflow). Boundary-off is byte-identical to the parent (regression-tested on logits).
- Phase 0 arms at the four May Recipe compute-optimal cells (d512/3.82e17, d768/2.81e18, d1024/1.16e19, d1280/3.46e19), v4-32 EP=1, with the README measurement conditions pinned (seq 4096, PKO on, long RoPE on, z-loss off, batch/steps from the README table).
- d512 runs both α ∈ {1.0, 0.707} ("alpha insurance"; paper's tuned values for Operator-1 and Loop-2). Winner by final macro loss proceeds.
- Gate 1: effective speedup > 1 at d512 and d768 vs the README baselines (3.5422 @ 433,986 tok/s; 3.2273 @ 294,726).
- Gate 2: d1024 + d1280, refit `loss(C) = 1.6 + A·C^−α̂`, projections must beat 2.534 @ 1e21 and 2.205 @ 1e23; fitted α̂ vs 0.0941 is secondary evidence.
- Cost: ≈45 v4-32 slice-hours for the full phase; ≈7–8 for gate 1 alone.

## Records

Runs land in W&B project `marin_moe`, group `moe-boundary`. Results and the go/no-go call get recorded here as each gate resolves.

**Final outcome (2026-09-29, matched recipe):** the measured loss wins at all four cells are confounded by an attention-window semantics change between the June baselines and the September variant runs, so the Phase 0 loss/speedup readout below is exploratory, not gate-grade. The one unconfounded result is throughput parity: the boundary operator costs ~0% at every scale (d1280 same-stack, same-window variant vs probe: 160,661 vs 160,924 tok/s, −0.16%).

The June 4 baselines ran short/long windows of 1024/2048 tokens (June code: `short = cfg.sliding_window // 2`, `long = cfg.sliding_window`, long rule `i % 4 == 3`), while the September variant runs used the current semantics — short 2048, long full-context, plus the last-layer long rule. Both eras log `sliding_window=2048`, so config matching did not catch it. Correcting for the window pattern, the September variant arms ran ~10% more real attention compute per token than the June baselines at every cell. Via the baseline law, that alone implies a loss win larger than the variant's measured wins, so the operator's measured Δloss cannot be separated from the window confound without a matched-window rerun.

| cell | variant macro | baseline macro | measured Δloss | window-implied Δloss | speedup (confounded) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| d512 3.82e17 | 3.5415 | 3.5422 | −0.0007 | −0.0179 | 1.005 |
| d768 2.81e18 | 3.2186 | 3.2273 | −0.0087 | −0.0136 | 1.050 |
| d1024 1.16e19 | 3.0129 | 3.0195 | −0.0066 | −0.0136 | 1.061 |
| d1280 3.46e19 | 2.8792 | 2.8857 | −0.0065 | −0.0120 | 1.054 |

- Gate 1 was recorded as passing; under the window confound that readout is exploratory. Gate 2's projection refit is equally confounded (the variant cells sit at higher real compute than the baseline law fit).
- α=1.0 beat α=0.707 at d512 (3.5415 vs 3.5459) — a within-era comparison; unaffected by the confound.
- The earlier "jax 0.9.2 → 0.11.1 stack drift" attribution for the d1280 throughput gap is retracted: controlled jax-version probes differ by 0.07%. The gap is now attributed to the window semantics change (#9529); a same-stack June-window probe is queued to quantify it.

- Training curves: [d1280 matched-pair report](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/reports/moe_boundary-d1280-matched-pair:-variant-vs-baseline--VmlldzoxODAyMDY5MQ==); variant runs `moe_boundary_compute_opt_d{512,768,1024,1280}_ep1_alpha1_matched`; June baselines `moe_may_compute_opt_d{512,768,1024,1280}_ep1`.

- Core entry state `BO(0, e) = α·e` (core starts from `h₀=0`), so feed `α·e` into the first core block.
- After the last core block, coda entry state `BO(h, e) = rms_norm(h) + α·e`.

**Debug ladder (per the replication plan):**
- **α insurance**: α=1.0 wins (−5.6e-3 vs 0.707). Paper Table 5 agrees (Operator-1 αemb=1).
- **LR re-centering**: ×1.0 is the best of {0.5, 1, 2} — the May Recipe heuristic LR is already centered for this model; the paper's transfer regret is not recoverable by GLR alone. (Paper's regret comes from the full Stage-1 chain: ELRM/HLRM/RM/OM/WD/WTE/UIS/schedule/Adam — most of these knobs don't exist in the MoE template's MuonH.)
- **Split ratio**: 2/2/2 at d6 is the paper's validated optimum (even P/C/D, remainders core-then-coda; Table 4/Fig 15a show alternatives are worse).

**Verdict**: under the May Recipe MoE with the recipe transferred from the Vanilla-equivalent baseline, the boundary operator alone does **not** beat the baseline at d512 (deficit +3.8e-3 loss; throughput parity within noise — arms span 350k–431k tok/s at identical compute). This is consistent with the paper's transfer-regret finding (Table 6: Operator-1 under Vanilla's recipe loses 7.8e-3 at base size and erases the exponent improvement, Fig. 16b). It does *not* refute the paper — we measured the transferred-recipe condition by design (recipe-matched comparability with the README baselines).

**Consequences:**
- Gate 1 cannot pass (requires speedup > 1 at both d512 and d768), so d768/d1024/d1280 arms were **not** launched — saves ~35 v4-32 slice-hours of a failing protocol.
- Phase A (looping/growth) is not justified on top of a failed Phase 0: the paper's bigger gains (Untied-Grow 1.6–2.7×) compound the same recipe-transfer risk, and each ladder point is ~10× the cost of Phase 0.

**Options going forward** (needs a decision):
1. **Close as negative result** — BO alone is not a promotable recipe change for this template under recipe-matched conditions. Cheapest; PR #9281 still lands the (well-tested, off≡baseline-verified) variant for future use.
2. **Recipe refit for the BO** (paper-style Stage-1 tuning at d512: β₁/β₂/ε/warmup/WD sweeps, ~8–10 arms ≈ 13–16 slice-hours) — tests whether the regret is recoverable in this template at all before deciding on Phase A.
3. **Skip to a combined arm** (e.g. Untied-2) at one matched cell — the paper's headline gains are there, but a single arm can't separate BO-from-looping contributions without Phase 0 passing.

🤖 **d1280 gate-2 cell finished — gate 2 fails, narrowly; the operator is a loss win at every scale.**

**What changed:** the d1280 (3.46e19 FLOPs) matched arm completed ([variant run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/moe_boundary_compute_opt_d1280_ep1_alpha1_matched) vs [baseline](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/moe_may_compute_opt_d1280_ep1), [matched-pair report](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/reports/moe_boundary-d1280-matched-pair:-variant-vs-baseline--VmlldzoxODAyMDY5MQ==)). It ran 14,324 steps after resuming from the step-2833 checkpoint (preempted at 2826); throughput was flat at ~159k tok/s across both TPU slices, so the preemption did not affect the measurement. Final macro loss **2.8792 vs baseline 2.8857** (−0.0065). The variant's eval curve is ahead of the baseline's at **every** eval point from step 2000 onward (e.g. 12k steps: 2.9485 vs 2.9544; 13k: 2.9122 vs 2.9199; 14k: 2.8835 vs 2.8907).

**Results (loss / median steady-state tok/s / effective speedup):**

| scale | variant | baseline | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| d512 3.82e17 | 3.5415 / 435.5k | 3.5422 / 434.8k | 1.005 |
| d768 2.81e18 | 3.2186 / 292.5k | 3.2273 / 294.8k | 1.050 |
| d1024 1.16e19 | 3.0129 / 222.0k | 3.0195 / 219.7k | 1.061 |
| d1280 3.46e19 | 2.8792 / 160.7k | 2.8857 / 171.9k | **0.987** |

Throughput here is the per-step median over steps ≥500 from full-resolution W&B history. This matters: these runs degrade over their final ~50 steps (the d512 variant collapses from 435k to 150–400k tok/s), which contaminates last-200-step averages — the earlier d512 "0.909 speedup / −9.4% overhead" reading was that artifact, not a real cost. Median-based, the operator is ~0% overhead at d512–d1024 (+0.2% / −0.8% / +1.0%).

**Gate verdict:**

- **Gate 1 passes** (d512 1.005, d768 1.050).
- **Gate 2 fails, on both criteria, but narrowly.** (a) d1280 effective speedup 0.987: the loss win (−0.0065) does not fully pay for the −6.5% steady-state throughput gap. (b) The 4-point refit `1.6 + 83.40·C^−0.0929` (α SE 0.0007) projects **+0.0026 worse at 1e21 and +0.0052 worse at 1e23** vs the baseline law `1.6 + 88.32·C^−0.0941` — despite the variant beating the baseline law at all four measured points (residuals −0.0155 / −0.0033 / −0.0065 / −0.0015). The fitted exponent is shallower (0.0929 vs 0.0941), so the extrapolation flips; cell residuals (±0.004) are the same order as the projection deltas, so this data does not resolve the flip.

**d1280 throughput anomaly.** The −6.5% is real and compute-bound: step duration 6.53 vs 6.10 s, identical logged FLOPs/token (3.29 GFLOP), loading/hook times negligible, flat across both TPU slices, MFU 12.0% vs 12.9%. Ruled out: remat config (the baseline predates the `remat_mode` knob — #6312, June 11 — and pre-knob code is `recompute_all` semantics, same effective remat), era/stack (September d1024 variant beat its June baseline by +1%), eval interference (0 of 108 slow steps align with evals, ~1.2% impact total). Leading hypothesis: the variant compiles at the HBM edge at d1280 — the restore OOM'd with 131 MB free of 32.9 GB — so the operator's extra activations push XLA over a memory threshold into worse fusion/spill choices. The natural follow-up is a `save_moe` remat or jmp-policy A/B at d1280.

**Bottom line:** the boundary operator is a consistent loss improvement at all four compute-optimal scales under the matched recipe, with ~zero throughput cost at d512–d1024 and a real −6.5% at d1280 that plausibly is a compile/memory artifact rather than intrinsic operator cost. As specified, gate 2's extrapolation criterion fails on a 0.0012 exponent difference that is within fit noise; the decision whether that warrants Phase 0.5 (memory-pressure follow-up) or promotion-as-recipe-change rests with @dlwh.

README updated in 907aab4fd0.

comments.body:
🤖 **Correction to the d1280 readout: the throughput gap is stack drift, not the boundary operator. The d1280 effective speedup is 1.054, and effective speedup passes at all four scales.**

**What changed:** we ran a fresh 64-step boundary-off probe of the d1280 baseline cell on today's stack ([moe_baseline_probe_d1280_ep1](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/moe_baseline_probe_d1280_ep1), launcher `launch_baseline_probe.py`). It measures **160,924 tok/s** median — essentially identical to the variant's 160,661 (−0.16%), and nowhere near the June README baseline's 171,910.

**Root cause:** the June baseline ran **jax 0.9.2 / libtpu 0.0.39**; September runs use **jax 0.11.1 / libtpu 0.0.46**. For this cell the current stack is **−6.4% slower** for both architectures. The d1024 comparison crossed the same stack boundary with no penalty (the September variant beat the June baseline by +1%), so the regression is specific to the d1280/batch-256 config — plausibly the same HBM-edge sensitivity that made the variant's restore OOM at 131 MB free, but it affects the baseline equally.

**Corrected d1280 numbers:**

| comparison | baseline tok/s | variant tok/s | effective speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| vs June README run (cross-stack) | 171,910 | 160,661 | 0.987 |
| vs same-stack probe (today) | 160,924 | 160,661 | **1.054** |

The four-cell picture is now: effective speedup **1.005 / 1.050 / 1.061 / 1.054** — passes everywhere, consistent with the operator costing ~0% wall-clock at every scale (the earlier d512 "−9.4% overhead" was separately a tail-measurement artifact).

**Gate 2 stands as before on the projection criterion:** the 4-point refit `1.6 + 83.40·C^−0.0929` extrapolates to +0.0026/+0.0052 worse than the baseline law at 1e21/1e23, despite the variant beating the baseline law at all four measured points. The margin-of-error on the variant's loss lead at d1280 (−0.0065, ahead at every eval point since step 2000) combined with ~zero throughput cost makes this a borderline gate-2 outcome that hinges entirely on the extrapolation, not on any measured disadvantage.

README updated in 03277e3bdf. My earlier memory-pressure explanation for the −6.5% was wrong; the probe result is the evidence.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Correction to the final readout above: the June baselines and September variant runs did not match on attention windows, despite matching on the logged config.

- June 4 baselines: short/long windows 1024/2048 (June code: `short = cfg.sliding_window // 2`, `long = cfg.sliding_window`, long rule `i % 4 == 3`).
- September variant runs: current semantics — short 2048, long full context, plus the last-layer long rule.
- Both eras log `sliding_window=2048`, so the config match did not catch it.

Correcting for window pattern, the variant arms ran ~10% more real attention compute per token than the June baselines at every cell. Via the baseline law, the windows alone imply a larger loss win than the variant measured (e.g. d1280: window-implied −0.0120 vs measured −0.0065), so the operator's Δloss cannot be separated from the window confound. The measured speedups (1.005/1.050/1.061/1.054) are confounded the same way, since they are computed at a fixed budget.

Two related corrections:
- The earlier "jax 0.9.2 → 0.11.1 stack drift" attribution for the d1280 throughput gap is retracted — controlled jax-version probes differ by 0.07% (#9529, now retitled to windows).
- The d1280 throughput parity measurement (variant 160,661 vs same-stack same-window probe 160,661 vs 160,924, −0.16%) is unaffected: both arms current-window.

Next step before any promotion decision: a matched-window rerun — variant and baseline on identical window semantics, same stack. The α=1.0 vs α=0.707 comparison is within-era and unaffected.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Window-probe update (follow-up to the correction above): the completed same-stack June-window probe measured 163,720 tok/s — 1.74% faster than current windows on the same stack, so windows explain only about a quarter of the historical d1280 throughput gap (6.4%). The remaining ~5.0% (171,910 June run vs 163,720 June-window September probe) is unexplained; jax is exonerated (0.07% in controlled probes) and a same-model `save_moe` remat recovery attempt OOM'd at this cell (retries stopped). A short profile is queued to look for a same-model speedup (#9529).

Two implications for this issue's readout:

1. **The window confound on loss is direction-solid but magnitude-open.** The +10.5% analytic attention FLOPs from the window change bought only +1.74% wall-clock at d1280, so the law-implied Δloss numbers in the correction comment (e.g. −0.0120 at d1280) are an upper bound on the compute channel; the receptive-field channel (what the windows do to what the model can see) is unmeasured and may dominate. The confound direction is unchanged — the variant arm is advantaged either way — but a matched-window rerun remains the only clean measurement.

2. **The variant-vs-baseline throughput parity result is unaffected.** 160,661 vs 160,924 (−0.16%) compares current-window arms on the same stack.

🤖 Research

The original May-recipe comparison is confounded by different attention-window semantics ([correction](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9280#issuecomment-5885050256)). Run paired d512 controls and α ∈ {1.0, 0.707} at seeds 0 and 1: 2,817 steps, batch 128, the same 16k data, optimizer, Paloma eval, 8×H100 region, and source revision. The disabled forward path is unchanged; 6- and 8-layer output/gradient reference tests and a bigram-source gradient check pass. comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Initialization investigation, while the unchanged d768 comparison runs:

The earlier d768 learning curve does show a crossover. Old α=1 treatment/control Paloma at approximately step1000 was 4.15230/4.14078 (+0.01152 loss), step2000 3.88258/3.88276 (tie), step8000 3.54149/3.55152 (−0.01003), and final 3.21856/3.22727 (−0.00871). [Treatment](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/moe_boundary_compute_opt_d768_ep1_alpha1_matched), [control](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/moe_may_compute_opt_d768_ep1). Their attention windows differed, so this observed trajectory does not isolate boundary-induced slow learning. Candidate-9 d512 showed no catchup by2817steps: α=1 halfway penalties +0.00983/+0.01766, final +0.01571/+0.01600 for seeds0/1.

Two mechanisms could contribute:

1. Coda enters with `RMSNorm(h_core) + α e_prelude`, while the core already contains the prelude signal. If those vectors initially align, the new injection emphasizes the prelude shortcut. Deeper layers may need training before their corrections become useful. This is a hypothesis; boundary activation/cosine measurements are needed.
2. The current candidate-9 operator resets AttnRes history to a single summary. The first core/coda attention gates therefore have only one source and cannot learn source-selection queries there. Final d512 α=1 seed0 query norms at these gates are zero, versus control0.34877/0.30485. The control still assigns the direct bigram source weights0.17433/0.14809 at those gates; the treatment has folded that source into its prelude summary. This is a concrete architectural change beyond a normalization/scale perturbation.

Recommended first initialization follow-up: keep the core injection at α=1, and replace the abrupt coda transform by `x=(1-g)h + g(RMSNorm(h)+αe)`, where h is the unnormalized core summary and e is the unnormalized prelude summary, with a predetermined schedule starting g=0 and reaching1 during roughly the first5% of training. That restores the current operator after warm-in. It starts closer to the baseline under zero-initialized uniform AttnRes queries, but is not exactly function-preserving because history resets still change query gradients. A scalar rescale of the whole sum is insufficient: the next branch RMSNorm removes it. Measure relative RMS and cosine alignment of the two terms instead; α=0.707 assumes independent signals if used as a variance argument, whereas their shared prelude signal makes independence doubtful and the actual correlation needs measurement.

Separately, test preserving the bigram as an individually retrievable AttnRes source after boundaries (e.g. sources `summary−bigram` and `bigram` retain the same total vector). That is an architecture ablation, not initialization alone. An exact baseline-preserving start would need to retain the full original history and gradually introduce the boundary transformation.

No initialization variant has been implemented or submitted. Finish the matched d768 arms first; then isolate coda warm-in before combining other changes.

spillover_issues.title: Agent MoE Experiment: boundary operator (prelude–core–coda, arXiv 2609.19107)

spillover_issues.author: ClassicLarry
spillover_issues.body:
This issue tracks iterative improvements to the Marin pretraining scaling ladder (`experiments/grug/fast_track`) using the **Marin Belay** process. It is a twist on autoresearch: an agent runs experiments in batches, and anyone can steer it with research directions. > **To suggest a research direction, comment on [Marin Belay Intake (#9514)](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9514).** Suggestions a maintainer approves (👍 from a `marin-devs` member) are copied into this thread automatically, and the agent acts only on this thread. This thread holds the agent's batch reports and maintainer steering. ![fast_track MoE ladder: Marin 535B baseline, clean KMA and candidate 9](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/d3b3f47e5cb788398150bb930adbad5701826c63/v1/ladder_scaling.png) The Marin 535B compute-optimal baseline follows `L(C) = 1.2 + 59.0·C^(−0.0843)` over four data-matched rungs. Clean KMA, the current baseline (★), is 0.022 lower at d512, 0.049 lower at d768, 0.040 lower at d1024 and 0.033 lower at d1280, which is about 1.14×, 1.43×, 1.40× and 1.35× the baseline's compute efficiency. Its dashed curve is fit to all four points: `L(C) = 1.2 + 64.8·C^(−0.0870)`. The **?** marks the open question this issue is chasing: how much further down each point can go. The red diamonds are the current best recipe, candidate 9 (Status below): **2.977 / 2.725 / 2.515** at d512 / d768 / d1024 (seed means at d512 and d768; the d768 bigram table follows rule A). d768 and d1024 are data-matched; d512 sits at its fixed-time step count (2817 vs 2383), so it's plotted slightly to the right. That is 0.157 / 0.098 / 0.078 below clean KMA, or about **2.1× / 2.2× / 2.0×** clean KMA's compute efficiency at the same FLOPs. The d1280 run is in progress. The right panel is clean KMA's training MFU at each rung on one 8×H100 node: 9.5% at d512 and d768, 12.2% at d1024, and 13.0% at d1280. FLOPs are counted from KMA's own layers (KDA, MLA + Inkling, AttnRes), as 3× forward with no recompute. The trainer's logged `throughput/mfu` uses the baseline architecture's FLOP formula, so it is slightly off for KMA. ## Objective **Minimize Paloma macro loss (`eval/paloma/macro_loss`, final step) at the d512 rung after a fixed 8 minutes of 8×H100 train-step time.** - **Fixed time, not fixed tokens.** Faster code trains on more tokens within the 8 minutes, so a pure speedup counts as a win. - The LR schedule depends on the step count, so fix steps before each run: `num_steps = round(480 s × ex/s ÷ batch)`. - Measure ex/s with a short `--no-eval` probe (~30 steps) on the same cluster, and use the steady-state throughput. - Compile, evals and startup are excluded from the 8 minutes. - **Numerics changes are allowed** (e.g. FP8, precision changes, approximate kernels). They count as ordinary wins; no parity check needed. - **Noise.** Differences under ~0.005 are noise. A win must beat the current best by more than 0.005. ### Gates (both relative to the current baseline, same fixed-time rule at each rung) - **Gate 1:** beat the baseline at d512 and d768. - **Gate 2:** also beat it at d1024 and d1280, **and** project to lower Paloma macro loss at 1e24 FLOPs. Fit a power law of final loss against training FLOPs across the four rungs, for both the baseline and the variant, fixing the asymptote to 1.2. ### Fixed - Training data, the 16k BPE tokenizer, and the eval sets. - Sequence length 4096. - One 8×H100 node per rung. - The FLOP accounting used for the gate-2 projection. ### Judgment calls - **Hero-scale speed is out of scope for v1, so use discretion.** - Robust target criteria would also check training speed and inference speed at hero scale. Marin Belay v1 skips those checks. - Judge whether a change's d512 gain would carry over to hero scale, and avoid changes whose gain comes from d512-only effects. Two examples: - Dropping MoE for dense would be a clear win at d512 because dense gets ~5× higher MFU there, but that MFU gain would not carry over at hero scale. - A much larger KV cache would also be a clear win at d512, but it would hurt long-context inference speed. - **Avoid magic numbers.** - Prefer changes with few new tuned constants. A tuned constant is justified when its gain is above the noise threshold and holds as a pattern across scales. For example, a 2× LR on one parameter group qualifies if it clears the noise threshold and the gain shows up consistently at larger rungs. - The higher a change's risk of curve fitting, the more scales it must be validated at before it counts as a win. - **Spend effort in proportion to an idea's likelihood of improvement.** - Promising ideas deserve several attempts. Long shots can be tried once and dropped. - A first run is not a verdict for a large change. If you try a new architecture or component, tune its optimizer assignment, LR, init and other key hyperparameters before concluding it doesn't work. Build from this branch. The recipe below covers every model and optimizer component. Values are for d512 unless noted; the code is `experiments/grug/fast_track/{model,optimizer,heuristic,launch}.py`. **Shape** | Rung | Width D | Layers | Local (KDA) / global (MLA) layers | Heads × head dim | Batch | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | d512 | 512 | 6 | 4 / 2 | 4 × 128 | 128 | | d768 | 768 | 8 | 6 / 2 | 6 × 128 | 128 | | d1024 | 1024 | 12 | 9 / 3 | 8 × 128 | 256 | | d1280 | 1280 | 14 | 10 / 4 | 10 × 128 | 256 | - Every 4th layer and the last layer are global; all other layers are local. - The run uses a 16k vocab and sequence length 4096 with packed documents. Every ShortConv and the KDA state respect document boundaries (the KDA state resets at each document start). - Weights are initialized with std 0.5/√D. Compute is bf16. **Embedding and output** - Token embedding → RMSNorm → GatedNorm. The result is AttnRes source 0. - Output path: final AttnRes gate → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → untied lm_head (`output_proj`). - The fused lm_head + cross-entropy loop uses a vocab tile of 8192. - GatedNorm (every GatedNorm in the model) is `x · sigmoid(W_up · SiLU(W_down · x))`, with a rank-128 bottleneck. **Block (every layer)** - **Attention sublayer:** input = its AttnRes gate mix → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → mixer (KDA or MLA). - **MoE sublayer:** input = its AttnRes gate mix → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → MoE → ShortConv on the MoE output. - Each ShortConv is a 4-tap causal depthwise conv. **Local layers: Kimi Delta Attention** (Kimi K3's layer) - **Projections:** q/k/v are D → N·128 with full heads (no GQA). Each goes through a ShortConv followed by SiLU. q and k are L2-normalized, and q is scaled by 1/√128. - **Decay:** per-channel log-decay `g = −5·sigmoid(exp(A_log)·(x·W_a_down·W_a_up + dt_bias))`. - The gate projection has rank 128. - `A_log` is one value per head, initialized to 0. - `dt_bias` is one value per channel, initialized so the decay rate spans 0.02–0.5. - **Write strength:** `β = sigmoid(x·W_β)`, one value per head. - **Recurrence:** `S_t = (I − β·k·kᵀ)·Diag(exp(g))·S_{t−1} + β·k·vᵀ`, read out as `o_t = S_tᵀ·q_t`. - It runs as chunked Pallas kernels, with a stable block-doubling inverse inside each chunk. - **Output:** per-head RMSNorm with a learnable 128-wide scale shared across heads → full-rank per-channel gate `sigmoid(x·W_g)` → `W_o`. - No positional encoding, no window, no XSA, and no ShortConv on the branch output. **Global layers: MLA + Inkling relative position** - **q:** full-rank, D → N·128 (no Q latent). - **k and v:** k = `W_uk · RMSNorm(x·W_dkv)` and v = `W_uv · RMSNorm(x·W_dkv)`. - They share one 512-wide KV latent, with a learnable RMSNorm on the latent. - Heads are 128 wide with no RoPE part. - There's no ShortConv on K, so the up-projections can be absorbed at inference. - **Scaling:** no QK-norm; `qk_mult` = 1, i.e. standard 1/√128 logit scaling. - **Position — Inkling relative-position bias**, added to the pre-softmax logits in place of RoPE: - `bias[h,i,j] = R[i,h,:] · P[:, i−j]`, where `R = x·W_r` is 16 values per head. - `P` is a bank of shape [16 × 1024] shared across heads. The relative extent is 1024. - It runs inside the FA4 attention kernel (forward, backward, and the SM90 backward pass). - **XSA** (exclusive self-attention): subtract the component of each head's output that is parallel to its own value vector. - **Output gate:** per head, `2·sigmoid(x·W_gate)`. `W_gate` is zero-initialized, so the gate is 1 at init. - The branch output also gets a ShortConv. **MoE sublayer (LatentMoE with quantile-balanced routing)** - **Experts:** 384 routed experts, top-8. Each is a SwiGLU with hidden size D/2. - **Latent space:** experts operate in a D/2-wide latent. The input goes through `W_latent_down` → RMSNorm, and the combined expert output goes back up through `W_latent_up`. - **Router:** reads the full-width token and computes logits in fp32. - Experts are selected by top-(8+1) on bias-adjusted logits, where the 9th logit is the threshold α. - Combine weights are the sigmoid of the unbiased logits, renormalized to sum to 2.5. - **Quantile balancing:** each step, each expert's threshold β is the global (1 − K/E) quantile of the logit margins (logit − α), read from a 10k-bin histogram. The router bias is set to −β. - The router bias is not trained by gradient. - **Capacity:** capacity factor 1.15, with pooled-wave expert-parallel dispatch. Receiver ranks are sort-based and the expand backward is gather-based. - **Shared experts:** 2 shared SwiGLU experts that bypass the latent: D → D/2 hidden → D. - **Fused projections:** - The router, latent-down, and both shared experts' gate/up projections run as one GEMM. - The shared experts' down-projections run as one GEMM. **Residual stream: Block Attention Residuals** - **Sources:** the embedding source, one running sum per completed block of sublayer outputs, and the running partial sum of the current block. - The model has 8 blocks. Block sums use the raw sublayer outputs. - **Gates:** every sublayer (attention and MoE) has its own gate, and there is one final gate before the output norm. Each gate has one learned pseudo-query `q ∈ ℝᴰ`, zero-initialized so every gate starts as a uniform average. - **Mixing:** per token, `logitᵢ = q · rms_norm(sourceᵢ)`, using a parameter-free (frozen) RMS key norm, then `softmax` over sources and a weighted sum of the raw sources. - **Implementation:** - Each completed block is scored once against every gate that reads it. - Backward: at d512 the layer's forward intermediates are saved. At d768–d1280 each layer is recomputed. At d1280 the attention branch is also rematerialized. - The model keeps one layer stack per mixer kind. **Optimizer** | Group | Update rule | LR | Parameters | |---|---|---|---| | `muonh` | MuonH | MuonH LR | all attention and MoE matrices: MLA `W_q`/`W_dkv`/`W_uk`/`W_uv`/`W_o`; KDA `W_q`/`W_k`/`W_v`/`W_o`/`W_g`; experts; shared experts; latent down/up. Also every GatedNorm `W_down`/`W_up`. | | `kda_beta` | MuonH | 2 × MuonH LR | KDA `W_β` | | `adamh` | AdamH | MuonH LR | lm_head (`output_proj`) | | `adam` | Adam | Adam LR | token embedding; router; attention output gate; router bias slot (overwritten by QB); all 1-D norm gains; ShortConv kernels; KDA `W_a_down`/`W_a_up`, `A_log`, `dt_bias`; Inkling `W_r` and `P` | | `attn_res_query` | Adam | 0.1 × Adam LR | the AttnRes pseudo-queries | - **MuonH:** Nesterov momentum 0.95 → Newton–Schulz orthogonalization (5 quintic steps, bucketed across same-shape matrices) → a step along that direction, then projection back onto the matrix's Frobenius sphere. Each matrix's norm stays fixed at its init value. - **AdamH:** the Adam direction with the same Frobenius-sphere (hyperball) projection. - **Adam:** β1 0.9. Only the router and the attention output gate get decoupled weight decay (0.02). comments.body:
Some ideas to get started. Treat this as a general pool of ideas, that indicates the spirit of what can be tried.
1. https://blog.tilderesearch.com/blog/online-kl-shampoo. Consider interactions with hyperball and selectively replace matrices.
2. Add a second embedding table with its own random init. Attn residuals queries both embedding tables, treating them as unique inputs.
3. Lets add value embeddings. That is, a second embedding table that gets added to V on the MLA layers. So take KV latent-> project to num_heads of size 128. Then do values = lambda1*values + lambda2*value_embeds[layer_i]. lambda 1 init to 1, lambda2 init to 0. value_embeds has [vocab_size, num_heads*head_dim, num_mla_layers] dimension. Can also try gated value embeds, where instead of lambda2, its conditional on residual stream via sigmoid(linear(x)).
4. Add learnable scalars to each submodule output, that feeds into attention residuals. May be worth tracking and plotting these in wandb, to see if indicates any architecture changes will help.
5. Try different variations of linear attention to replace KDA.
6. It has been shown in many places that the final couple layers of attention dont prefer to attend to outputs from the final MLPs. See if there is any change to attention residuals to help make this more natural.
7. Adding an lm_head auxillary loss to the output of layer 1 for the first X (say 500) steps can help give the routed experts a cleaner role early. Unclear how this interacts with attention residuals.
8. Hash routing on first layer.
9. Instead of Adam/AdamH on embed and lm_head, look into other optimizers here that have shown promise in literature.
10. Do any weights benefit from extremely different beta1/beta2/momentum terms, or swapping their optimizer group.
11. Update the router behavior (sigmoid vs softmax), normalizing over picked experts vs not, sampling over experts instead of top k).
12. Null routing (enable tokens to select null experts which skips their computation, dynamic compute per token).
13. Multi-token-prediction.
14. Sparse attention.

If users give comments with singular specific ideas, give it priority over this laundry list.

🤖 **Batch 1: cheap architecture adds from the idea list, an LR check, and a noise and profile baseline** (d512, 2475 steps) — **done**

**Goal.** Test the lowest-cost ideas from @ClassicLarry's list: `#2` (second embedding table), `#3` (value embeddings, both forms), and `#4` (learnable sublayer output scalars, logged to W&B). Also check whether the `MoeHeuristic` LR, which was fit on the old baseline architecture, is still right for KMA (×1.5 and ×0.67 on both LRs). Add a seed-1 baseline to calibrate noise, and a 60-step profile to find speed levers. Speed counts as a win under the fixed-time objective.

**Assumption (I'll correct it next batch if it's wrong).** None of these changes adds meaningful compute, so all runs use the baseline's 2475 steps instead of a separate probe. After each run I check its steady-state ex/s. If it is more than about 1% below 660, I rerun at `round(480 × ex/s / 128)` steps. Branch [`ladderclimb_v1_batch01`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/eb26f3cbc9) @ `eb26f3cbc9`: every change is gated by a `--model-set` / `--opt-set` flag and defaults to off.

**Implementation details**
- **ve:** each MLA layer gets a [16384 × N·128] table, and `v = λ1·v + λ2·VE[token]` (λ1 = 1, λ2 = 0 at init). The tables, λ and the gate go to Adam at the Adam LR, like `token_embed`.
- **veg:** `v = λ1·v + sigmoid(x·W)·VE[token]`, with one gate per head. `W` is zero-initialized, so the gate starts at 0.5.
- **osc:** a scalar initialized to 1 on each attention and MoE sublayer output before it enters the AttnRes history (Adam). Logged as `train/attn_res/scale_{attn,mlp}_L*`.
- **emb2:** a second randomly initialized table → learnable RMSNorm, prepended as an extra AttnRes block that every gate can read.

**Takeaway.**
- **Noise is the story.** The identical-code seed-1 baseline landed at 3.1195, 0.0056 below seed 0. Against the two-seed baseline mean of 3.1223, none of the architecture changes clears noise: emb2 −0.005, veg −0.004, osc −0.002, ve −0.002. ve, veg and emb2 also ran 7–13% slower, so at a fair 8-minute step count they would lose part of that.
- **The LR heuristic holds for KMA.** Both ×1.5 and ×0.67 are clearly worse.
- **The learned scalars in osc point at the MoE output.** Its final values: MoE outputs grow to 1.2 / 1.4 / 1.5 / 2.1 / 1.7 / 1.9× by layer, the early KDA outputs shrink to 0.48×, and the MLA outputs stay near 1.0. The routed-expert output magnitude is capped by MuonH's sphere and the 2.5 combine renorm, and it wants to grow.
- **Profile (8×H100, d512, ~187 ms/step).** Compute is ~155 ms: elementwise fusions ~61, GEMMs ~43, sort/scatter/gather ~23, KDA ~14, FA4 ~7. Exposed EP all-to-all is ~18 ms, and the host gap between steps is ~6 ms.
  - **One kernel is a bug:** the token-embedding gradient takes **~11 ms/step**. Under the bf16 compute policy, the gather's transpose scatter-adds every token's cotangent directly into a **bf16** table. That means contended bf16 atomics, with frequent tokens' gradients rounded at every add. A single-GPU microbenchmark puts the fp32 scatter at 0.2 ms. The same scatter is why ve, veg and emb2 were slow: each extra table adds one.

- Test MoE output-magnitude variants: combine renorm sum 2.5 → 4, sigmoid without renorm, softmax combine, and K3's normalized LatentMoE.
- In response to the literature-scan comment: a background scan turned up these candidates for later batches: K3 normalized LatentMoE, per-head Muon, NorMuon-style row normalization, Engram n-gram memory, null experts, and FP8 lm_head.
**Next batch (tentative):** act on the profile. Validate any win above 0.005 at d768. Try combinations of the winners, MTP, and router variants (`#11`).

Gate 2 (d1024/d1280) will run once on the bundled winners, to save slots.

**Takeaway .**
- **New base at 2817 steps: 3.0987 / 3.0992, mean 3.0990.** That is −0.023 vs the original baseline's two-seed mean, with no architecture change. The only change is the fp32 embedding backward plus the step count its speed allows.

- **emb2: −0.0036.** That is its third consistent ~−0.004. **min LR 0: −0.0030.** Both are below the noise bar alone, so batch 4 stacks them with qk_mult (2 seeds).

  - The early aux lm_head loss (`#7`): **+0.016**. A lighter retry is queued: weight 0.3 over 200 steps.

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 **Batch 5: @ClassicLarry's three requests: z-loss weight, projection biases, and freezing QB at 50%** (d512, 2817 steps; reference = batch-3 base mean **3.0990**)

**Addresses** the comment asking to vary the logit z-loss, add biases to some weight matrices, and freeze QB updates halfway through training. All runs build on the fp32-embedding base, branch [`ladderclimb_v1_batch05`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/ea0592bd02).
- **z-loss:** the current weight is 1e-4 (`--z-loss-weight`). One run turns it off, one raises it 10×.
- **Biases:** zero-initialized and trained with Adam, at three sites:
  - Qwen-style q/k/v: KDA q/k/v before their ShortConvs, and MLA q plus the KV latent before its RMSNorm.
  - The attention sublayer output.
  - The MoE sublayer output.

  If the combined run moves, I'll split the sites next batch.
- **QB freeze:** from step 1408 on, the router bias keeps its last quantile-balanced value (`qb_freeze_step`). Routing can then drift, and load balance is no longer enforced.

| change | branch@commit | W&B | steps | ex/s | mid loss | final Paloma macro loss | Δ vs 3.0990 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| z-loss weight 0 (vs 1e-4) | [`ea0592bd02`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/ea0592bd02) | [lc1-b05-z0](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b05-z0) | 2817 | 751 | 3.3902 | 3.0966 | −0.0024 |
| z-loss weight 1e-3 | [`ea0592bd02`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/ea0592bd02) | [lc1-b05-z1e3](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b05-z1e3) | 2817 | 749 | 3.4029 | 3.1046 | +0.0056 |
| biases: q/k/v + attention out + MoE out | [`ea0592bd02`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/ea0592bd02) | [lc1-b05-bias](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b05-bias) | 2817 | 742 (−1%) | 3.3913 | 3.0993 | +0.0003 |
| freeze QB router biases at step 1408 (50%) | [`ea0592bd02`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/ea0592bd02) | [lc1-b05-qbfrz](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b05-qbfrz) | 2817 | 751 | 3.3924 | 3.1059 | +0.0069 |
| **AttnRes logit bias** per (gate, source), zero-init, Adam at 0.1× (human, 2nd comment) | [`f1734ddcdf`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/f1734ddcdf) | [lc1-b05-arb](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b05-arb) | 2817 | 751 | 3.3954 | 3.1001 | +0.0011 |
| AttnRes logit bias + AttnRes z-loss 1e-3 | [`f1734ddcdf`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/f1734ddcdf) | [lc1-b05-arbz3](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b05-arbz3) | 2817 | 748 | 3.3996 | 3.1045 | +0.0055 |
| AttnRes logit bias + AttnRes z-loss 1e-1 | [`f1734ddcdf`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/f1734ddcdf) | [lc1-b05-arbz1](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b05-arbz1) | 2817 | 746 | 3.4570 | 3.1475 | +0.0485 |

**AttnRes logit bias and z-loss** (added for the follow-up comment). Each of the 13 gates gets a zero-init bias per source it reads: one per completed block, plus one for the running partial. It is added to the logit before the softmax and trained with Adam at 0.1× the Adam LR, the same as the queries. The z-loss is the mean over tokens of logsumexp(gate logits)², averaged over gates, and added to the loss. Every run now logs the pseudo-query norms: `train/attn_res/query_norm_{mean,max,gNN}` plus the unweighted `train/attn_res/z`. One caveat: a z-loss can be satisfied by shifting a gate's biases down together, which leaves the mix unchanged. I'll compare the q norms across the three runs.

**Correction:** the AttnRes z-loss runs' eval losses also included the z-loss term (the same bug, found in batch 18). That inflated them by weight × z: about +0.0012 for 1e-3 and +0.001 for 1e-1. Their deltas are about +0.004 and +0.047 instead of +0.0055 and +0.0485, so both are still worse.

**Takeaway (all done).**
- **AttnRes logit bias is neutral (+0.0011).**
- **The AttnRes z-loss hurts:** +0.0055 at 1e-3 and +0.049 at 1e-1.
- **It raises the pseudo-query norms rather than lowering them.** Final values:

  | run | AttnRes z (unweighted) | query norm mean | query norm max |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | bias only | 6.31 | 0.227 | 0.377 |
  | bias + z 1e-3 | 1.23 | 0.286 | 0.583 |
  | bias + z 1e-1 | 0.01 | 0.332 | 0.565 |

  The z-loss is minimized by pushing every logit down. With keys that are RMS-normalized but not mean-centred, the query does this by growing along the direction opposite the common component of the sources, instead of shifting all biases together. That distorts the mix.
- The other results from this batch:
  - Freezing QB at 50%: +0.007.
  - lm_head z-loss 1e-3: +0.006.
  - lm_head z-loss 0: −0.002.
  - Projection biases: neutral.

🤖 **Batch 8: shared → routed expert FLOPs (human request), and seed-matched bases for paired comparisons** (d512)

**Addresses** @ClassicLarry's comment: **1 shared expert, top-10 routed** instead of 2 shared and top-8. The swap is FLOP-neutral: one shared SwiGLU (3·512·256) equals two latent routed experts (2·3·256·256). It is **8% slower**, though (80-step probe: 693.5 vs 754.1 ex/s), because the EP all-to-all carries 25% more assignments. So it runs at 2591 fixed-time steps, compared paired against the seed-0 qk_mult-2.5 base (3.0858).

Also running: seed-matched bases for the paired protocol described in batch 7, and a stack of the two best paired settings from batch 7.

| change | branch@commit | W&B | steps | ex/s | mid loss | final Paloma macro loss | Δ (paired) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 shared + top-10 routed (qk_mult 2.5) | [`03900b76d6`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/03900b76d6) | [lc1-b08-sh1k10](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b08-sh1k10) | 2591 | 691 | 3.4054 | 3.1006 | **+0.0148** |
| fp32 base, seed 2 | [`03900b76d6`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/03900b76d6) | [lc1-b08-base-s2](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b08-base-s2) | 2817 | 751 | 3.3995 | 3.1057 | reference |
| fp32 base, seed 3 | [`03900b76d6`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/03900b76d6) | [lc1-b08-base-s3](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b08-base-s3) | 2817 | 748 | 3.4025 | 3.1018 | reference |
| qk_mult 2.5, seed 3 | [`03900b76d6`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/03900b76d6) | [lc1-b08-qk25-s3](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b08-qk25-s3) | 2817 | 747 | 3.3946 | 3.0917 | **−0.0101** vs base s3 |
| qk_mult 2.5 + Adam β1 0.8 + lm_head z-loss 0 | [`03900b76d6`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/03900b76d6) | [lc1-b08-ab08z0](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b08-ab08z0) | 2817 | 746 | 3.3705 | **3.0805** | **−0.0053** |
| qk 2.5 + β1 0.8 + z-loss 0, seed 1 | [`c2803601b0`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/c2803601b0) | [lc1-b08-ab08z0-s1](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b08-ab08z0-s1) | 2817 | 745 | 3.3753 | 3.0872 | −0.0023 vs 3.0895 |
| qk 2.5 + β1 0.8 + z-loss 0, seed 2 | [`c2803601b0`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/c2803601b0) | [lc1-b08-ab08z0-s2](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b08-ab08z0-s2) | 2817 | 746 | 3.3879 | 3.0973 | −0.0060 vs 3.1033 |
| qk 2.5 + β1 0.8 + z-loss 0, seed 3 | [`c2803601b0`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/c2803601b0) | [lc1-b08-ab08z0-s3](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b08-ab08z0-s3) | 2817 | 752 | 3.3767 | 3.0867 | −0.0050 vs 3.0917 |

**qk_mult 2.5, paired over 4 seeds:**

| seed | fp32 base | qk_mult 2.5 | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 3.0987 | 3.0858 | −0.0129 |
| 1 | 3.0992 | 3.0895 | −0.0097 |
| 2 | 3.1057 | 3.1033 | −0.0024 |
| 3 | 3.1018 | 3.0917 | −0.0101 |
| **mean** | 3.1014 | 3.0926 | **−0.0088 ± 0.0022 (SE)** |

The base seeds alone span 0.007, and a single seed can mislead: seed 2's gain is only −0.002. Pairing by seed, which shares the data order, is what makes the gain clear.

**β1 0.8 + lm_head z-loss 0 on top of qk 2.5, paired over 4 seeds: −0.0053 / −0.0023 / −0.0060 / −0.0050, mean −0.0047 ± 0.0008 (SE).** Every seed gains and the spread is tight. The mean sits just under the 0.005 bar, but the paired SE makes it a real if small effect. It costs nothing, so I'm including it in the gate-2 bundle, flagged as borderline.

**Takeaway.**
- **1 shared + top-10 routed is worse at fixed time: +0.0148.** The FLOPs are unchanged, but 25% more routed assignments make the EP all-to-all and dispatch 8% slower (691 vs 751 ex/s), so it trains 226 fewer steps. At d512 the step time is bound by communication and dispatch rather than FLOPs, which is a case where d512 may not reflect hero scale. I'm not pursuing it further at this rung.

comments.author: neel04
comments.body: Try a simple version of looped models (w/ and wo/ growing, a la https://github.com/qlabs-eng/slowrun/pull/92 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19107) with untying and see if that improves performance. Make sure to include the input injection as well!

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 **Batch 9: looped models (@neel04's request): tied looping, with and without growth, with input injection** (d512, paired seed 0 vs qk_mult-2.5 base **3.0858**)

**Addresses** @neel04's comment. It follows [slowrun#92](https://github.com/qlabs-eng/slowrun/pull/92) (1× for 70% of training, then 2×) and [arXiv 2609.19107](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19107) (boundary operator `Norm(h) + α·e`, growth partway through training, backprop through all passes, and FLOPs of every pass counted). Branch [`ladderclimb_v1_batch09`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/c2803601b0).

**How it maps onto KMA** (`loop_passes`, `loop_grow_step`):
- **The looped core is the whole 6-layer stack**, weights tied. Each pass extends the Block AttnRes history. Pass 2's gates read the embedding, every pass-1 block, and the pass-2 blocks so far. Pass 2 has its own zero-initialized AttnRes pseudo-queries, so its gates start as uniform averages over that longer history.
- **Input injection.** At the start of each extra pass, the running partial is initialized to `α·e`, where e is the normalized embedding source and α is learned (init 1, Adam), and the pass's layers write onto it. The AttnRes gates already see e as source 0. This is the explicit re-injection from both references. The AttnRes softmax already normalizes what each sublayer reads, which plays the part of `Norm(h)`.
- **Growth** uses a step-gated `lax.cond`. Before the growth step only pass 1 executes, at full base speed. After it both passes run, with gradients through both. The router biases are shared per physical layer; their QB statistics are averaged over the passes.
- **Fixed-time steps.** Two passes run at 0.506× the base throughput (80-step probe: 381.8 vs 754.1 ex/s), so every run is given 8 minutes of train-step time:
  - loop2 throughout: 1426 steps.
  - Grow at 70%: N solves `0.7N/751 + 0.3N/380 = 480/128`, so N = 2179 and growth is at step 1525.
  - Grow at 50%: N = 1892, growth at step 946.
- **Not in this batch: untied growth**, where the core is copied at the growth step and the copies train separately. It changes the parameter tree and optimizer state mid-run, so it needs trainer work. It's next if tied growth looks promising.

| change | branch@commit | W&B | steps | ex/s | mid loss | final Paloma macro loss | Δ (paired) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| loop ×2 throughout (tied, injection) | [`c2803601b0`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/c2803601b0) | [lc1-b09-loop2](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b09-loop2) | 1426 | 381 | 3.5052 | 3.1766 | **+0.0908** |
| grow 1→2 passes at 70% of steps (step 1525) | [`c2803601b0`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/c2803601b0) | [lc1-b09-grow70](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b09-grow70) | 2179 | | | OOM: 79.8 GiB (lax.cond kept both branches' buffers); fixed, rerun below | |
| grow 1→2 passes at 50% (step 946) | [`c2803601b0`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/c2803601b0) | [lc1-b09-grow50](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b09-grow50) | 1892 | | | OOM: 79.8 GiB (lax.cond kept both branches' buffers); fixed, rerun below | |
| grow 1→2 at 70% (step 1525), static per-phase programs | [`0d023baad9`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/0d023baad9) | [lc1-b09-grow70b](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b09-grow70b) | 2179 | 747 → 380 | 3.5435* | 3.1065 | +0.0207 |
| grow 1→2 at 50% (step 946), static per-phase programs | [`0d023baad9`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/0d023baad9) | [lc1-b09-grow50b](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b09-grow50b) | 1892 | 747 → 380 | 3.5647* | 3.1195 | +0.0337 |

The mid-run eval always runs every pass, so for the growth runs the mid loss evaluates a model that has not trained its second pass yet. Only the final loss is comparable.

**Takeaway.**
- **Looping loses at d512 fixed time**, in every variant:

  | variant | Δ |
  |---|---|
  | 2× throughout | +0.091 |
  | grow 1→2 at 50% | +0.034 |
  | grow 1→2 at 70% | +0.021 |

  The less time spent in the 2× slower phase, the smaller the loss. The measured phase throughputs, 747 then 380 ex/s, match the budget, so all three got 8 minutes. \* marks mid losses from evals that ran both passes before the second pass had trained.
- **Why it loses.** The paper's gains are compute multipliers at ≥1e20 FLOPs with 7–8 tokens per parameter for its growth variants. Here the whole run is about 1e17 FLOPs and data-limited: in 8 minutes the model sees only about 1.1B tokens. An extra pass costs tokens, which are the scarce resource at this rung. Untied growth has the same FLOP cost after growth, so I'm not building it for d512. It is a better fit for a hero-scale study.

**Earlier notes.**
- **Fixed 2× looping throughout is much worse at fixed time: +0.091.** It gets only 1426 steps. At d512, one pass of the 6-layer stack is not the bottleneck; tokens seen are.
- **The growth runs first OOMed.** The step-gated `lax.cond` allocated 79.8 GiB, because XLA holds buffers for both branches. I replaced it with two statically compiled train steps, a one-pass program before the growth step and a two-pass one after, chosen per step in Python ([`0d023baad9`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/0d023baad9)). Its CPU check matches the plain model exactly.

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body: Let’s try slimming some things down. Drop the gated norm on embed, gated norm on lm head, and make the attn gate on kda just per head instead of per channel. Try these independently.

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 **Batch 10: slimming ablations (@ClassicLarry's request)** (d512, 2817 steps, paired seed 0 vs the qk_mult-2.5 base **3.0858**)

**Addresses** the comment asking to drop the GatedNorm on the embedding, drop the GatedNorm on the lm_head input, and make the KDA output gate per head instead of per channel. Each runs independently on top of qk_mult 2.5. All three remove compute, so running them at the base's 2817 steps slightly under-credits them, which is the conservative direction.
- `embed_gated_norm=false`: embedding → RMSNorm only.
- `final_gated_norm=false`: final AttnRes gate → RMSNorm → lm_head.
- `kda_gate_per_head=true`: `W_g` becomes [D, N] instead of [D, N·128], and `σ(x W_g)` is broadcast over each head's 128 channels. It stays on MuonH, like `W_β`.

| change | branch@commit | W&B | steps | ex/s | mid loss | final Paloma macro loss | Δ (paired) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no GatedNorm on the embedding | [`afa837be5f`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/afa837be5f) | [lc1-b10-noembgn](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b10-noembgn) | 2817 | 748 | 3.3773 | 3.0863 | +0.0005 |
| no GatedNorm before the lm_head | [`afa837be5f`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/afa837be5f) | [lc1-b10-nofingn](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b10-nofingn) | 2817 | 749 | 3.3822 | 3.0864 | +0.0006 |
| KDA output gate per head (not per channel) | [`afa837be5f`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/afa837be5f) | [lc1-b10-kdagh](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b10-kdagh) | 2817 | 705 (−6%, see below) | 3.3877 | 3.0912 | **+0.0054** |
| both GatedNorms removed (embedding + lm_head input) | [`0d023baad9`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/0d023baad9) | [lc1-b10-nogn2](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b10-nogn2) | 2817 | 752 | 3.3803 | **3.0821** | **−0.0037** |

**Takeaway.**
- **Both GatedNorm removals are neutral** (+0.0005 embedding, +0.0006 lm_head input), so they are free simplifications. **Removing both gives 3.0821 (−0.0037)**, so they stack. The model is simpler and, if anything, better. The batch-12 bundle drops both.
- **The per-head KDA output gate is worse: +0.0054 at the same 2817 steps.** The per-channel gate carries information. It also ran 6% slower, because my `jnp.repeat` broadcast of the gate didn't fuse; a reshape to `[B, S, N, 128]` would avoid that. The step count was the same as the base, so the loss comparison is fair either way. Not pursuing it.

comments.author: AMX07
comments.body:
try NoPE on the MLA layers (drop Inkling), following Kimi K3 [https://github.com/MoonshotAI/Kimi-K3/blob/main/k3_tech_report.pdf](url)

K3 and Kimi Linear both pair KDA with NoPE MLA, relying on KDA's recurrent decay for position. KMA already has the same pieces (KDA before every MLA layer, q/k/v ShortConvs), so Inkling may be redundant here.

From Opus 5.5:

**Implementation (small):**

- `GrugModelConfig.__post_init__`: remove the `mla requires inkling_relpos` check. MLA layers are all global, so `disable_rope=True` there, and removing `rel_pos` gives pure NoPE (no RoPE, no bias).
- `CausalSelfAttention.init`, MLA branch: `rel_pos=InklingRelPos.init(...) if cfg.inkling_relpos else None`.
- Check that the optimizer group routing Inkling `W_r`/`P` to Adam doesn't break when they're absent.

**Runs (d512, paired seed 0 vs the qk_mult-2.5 base, 3.0858):**
1. NoPE, qk_mult 2.5, steps from its own ex/s probe.
2. NoPE, qk_mult 2.0 and 3.5 (the current optimum was tuned with Inkling present).
3. Diagnostic: NoPE token-matched at 2817 steps, to separate "learns as well" from "trains faster."
4. If it loses slightly, try NoPE + ShortConv on MLA q only (keeps W_uk absorbable).

Replicate on seeds 1–2 if it clears 0.005 paired.

**For gate 2:** `attn_res_remat_attention` is forced on at d1280 partly because of the `[B, H, S, W]` Inkling bias. NoPE might let that remat be dropped at larger rungs, which is an extra speed gain there.

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 **Batch 11: NoPE MLA, dropping Inkling (@AMX07's request) — done** (d512, paired seed 0 vs the qk_mult-2.5 base **3.0858**)

**Addresses** @AMX07's comment. Kimi K3 and Kimi Linear pair KDA with NoPE MLA and rely on KDA's decay for position; KMA already has KDA before every MLA layer. With `inkling_relpos=false`, the MLA layers are pure NoPE: they are all global, where RoPE is already off. The optimizer routing is unaffected, and the KDA tests and CPU smoke tests pass. Dropping the bias speeds up FA4, so the NoPE runs get **+2.4%** more steps (80-step probe: 772.5 vs 754.1 ex/s → 2886 fixed-time steps).

| change | branch@commit | W&B | steps | ex/s | mid loss | final Paloma macro loss | Δ (paired) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NoPE, throughput probe | [`edc8f0cde0`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/edc8f0cde0) | [lc1-b11p-nope](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b11p-nope) | 80 | 772.5 | — | — | — |
| NoPE, qk_mult 2.5 (fixed-time) | [`0d023baad9`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/0d023baad9) | [lc1-b11-nope](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b11-nope) | 2886 | 769 | 3.3918 | 3.0891 | +0.0033 |
| NoPE, qk_mult 2.0 | [`0d023baad9`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/0d023baad9) | [lc1-b11-nope-qk20](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b11-nope-qk20) | 2886 | 768 | 3.3917 | 3.0959 | +0.0101 |
| NoPE, qk_mult 3.5 | [`0d023baad9`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/0d023baad9) | [lc1-b11-nope-qk35](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b11-nope-qk35) | 2886 | 764 | 3.3867 | 3.0884 | +0.0026 |
| NoPE, token-matched diagnostic | [`edc8f0cde0`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/edc8f0cde0) | [lc1-b11-nope-tm](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b11-nope-tm) | 2817 | 770 | 3.3905 | 3.0948 | +0.0090 |
| NoPE + ShortConv on MLA q, qk_mult 2.5 | [`4b9b01f54b`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/4b9b01f54b) | [lc1-b11-nopeqc](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b11-nopeqc) | 2880 | 767 | 3.3925 | 3.0880 | +0.0022 |
| NoPE + ShortConv on MLA q, qk_mult 3.0 | [`4b9b01f54b`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/4b9b01f54b) | [lc1-b11-nopeqc-qk30](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b11-nopeqc-qk30) | 2880 | 766 | 3.3842 | 3.0876 | +0.0018 |
| Inkling (kept) + ShortConv on MLA q | [`4b9b01f54b`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/4b9b01f54b) | [lc1-b11-inkqc](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b11-inkqc) | 2817 | 740 (−1.5%) | 3.3843 | 3.0881 | +0.0023 |

**Takeaway.**
- **NoPE MLA is roughly on par with Inkling at d512: +0.002 to +0.003, not better.**
  - qk_mult 2.5 and 3.5 score +0.0033 and +0.0026.
  - qk_mult 2.0 is clearly worse, at +0.0101.
  - So the qk_mult optimum found with Inkling holds without it.
- **The token-matched run separates the two effects.** At equal steps NoPE is **+0.009** worse, so Inkling helps learning by about 0.009 per step, and NoPE's +2.4% speed wins back about 0.006 of that.
- **ShortConv on MLA q** (K3's layout; W_uk stays absorbable) brings NoPE a bit closer (+0.0022 / +0.0018), but not past Inkling. On top of Inkling it does not help (+0.0023) and costs 1.5% throughput.
- **Verdict:** keep Inkling. Same-seed reruns differ by about 0.002, so this whole batch sits within about one noise unit of the base. NoPE is still worth a look at d1280, where dropping the `[B, H, S, W]` bias could remove the forced attention remat and speed that rung up. I'll check it when gate 2 is underway.

(All runs in this batch waited through the 23:59–01:20 UTC preemption before starting.)
